## Problem
Repeated chat navigation and group switching in the real-account Firefox journey exhausts the five concurrent SSE connections per account and returns HTTP 429 while only the current chat and unread observer should remain open (Refs #551). Client subscriptions call EventSource.close(), and the production web proxy destroys its upstream when the downstream closes. The PWA service worker's forwarded fetch prevents cancellation from reaching the upstream: an isolated trusted-HTTPS Firefox A/B with the actual worker retained five streams and rejected eleven reconnections; bypassing only realtime SSE GETs closed all sixteen streams across eight group switches, with at most two active and zero rejections. Neither variant cached API responses.

## Expected
Closing or switching a chat releases the old realtime connections. Realtime SSE GETs remain browser-owned network requests, with server authorization and the five-connection limit preserved. Other private API/media requests keep their no-cache and offline fail-closed behavior.

## How to check
Run the existing focused PWA and proxy tests, adding coverage for repeated full-chat/unread stream switching, connection closure, and private response cache exclusion. Confirm the isolated Firefox A/B and have the parent coordinate the unchanged real-account suite. title: Verify the current hosted Safari and Home Screen app integrations once

body:
## Problem

The benchmark still requires 180×320 film output, although the current compiler emits a 720×1280 group film. Its tests even treat width 720 as a failure. This issue repairs the measurement contract; **it must not lower capture resolution, retro-processing quality or retained individual-clip quality.**

Current dev `a1dc77e` has distinct media stages:

| Stage | Existing behavior to preserve |
| --- | --- |
| Browser capture | Requests 1920×1080 at ideal 30 fps; the browser chooses the supported size/orientation. Recording requests 8 Mbps video and 128 kbps audio. |
| Browser retro video | Fits within a 1920-pixel long edge / 1080-pixel short edge without upscaling; preserves portrait and landscape. |
| Server processed individual video | Keeps source dimensions and rate; client-processed looks are not applied twice. |
| Photo-derived film segment | 720×1280. This is separate from original photo capture/browser grading. |
| Compiled group film | 720×1280 at 30 fps; landscape letterboxed, with existing Safari-compatible H.264/color handling and normalized audio. |

Evidence: [capture](https://github.com/Collaboration95/rewind-app/blob/a1dc77e940a824b0d4e9ffaabf1e4ac517e38816/src/capture/platform.ts#L562), [browser retro](https://github.com/Collaboration95/rewind-app/blob/a1dc77e940a824b0d4e9ffaabf1e4ac517e38816/src/capture/retro-browser.ts#L307), [individual clip processing](https://github.com/Collaboration95/rewind-app/blob/a1dc77e940a824b0d4e9ffaabf1e4ac517e38816/server/src/ffmpeg.ts#L230), [film compilation](https://github.com/Collaboration95/rewind-app/blob/a1dc77e940a824b0d4e9ffaabf1e4ac517e38816/server/src/ffmpeg.ts#L491), [obsolete assertion](https://github.com/Collaboration95/rewind-app/blob/a1dc77e940a824b0d4e9ffaabf1e4ac517e38816/scripts/measure-real-group-performance.mjs#L58). #419 records the 1080p browser retro path. Commit `5bc0c68` introduced 720p films separately.

#353 correctly measured historical SQLite/loopback conditions. Its timings do not establish current 720p-film/PostgreSQL performance. The benchmark's synthetic 720p input fixture is not a product-wide capture ceiling.

## Expected

- Update benchmark assertions/fixtures to validate the actual compiled-film contract. Correct output passes; wrong dimensions fail.
- Keep changes within measurement code, its tests and measurement documentation. Do not modify production media processing or capture settings to make a benchmark pass.
- Preserve input counts/duration, chronology, decoding, audio, privacy, bounded runtime and failure assertions.
- Refresh the bounded five-member measurements on current code. Declare database, storage and workload; distinguish local SQLite, isolated PostgreSQL and any separately authorized hosted result.
- Keep the existing API p95 ≤2 s target excluding external IdP latency, and compilation ≤10 min for 25 new six-second clips / 150 seconds. Record actual misses rather than lowering media quality.
- A 1080p source remains a 1080p processed/downloadable individual clip. Film composition may apply its existing 720p output contract. Preserve portrait/landscape handling and avoid double retro treatment.

## How to check

1. Run `node --test scripts/measure-real-group-performance.test.mjs`; assert valid current film output succeeds and obsolete/wrong output fails.
2. Run `npm run test:focused -- frontend tests/retro-looks.test.ts` and `npm run test:focused -- server server/tests/film-compilation.test.mjs` to protect current processing and compatibility behavior.
3. Include a bounded generated 1080×1920 and 1920×1080 source check: individual processing retains dimensions/audio; film compilation produces its existing 720×1280 output. Do not relabel these as physical-camera evidence.
4. Run the repaired workload on built current code and `npm run test:fast`. Retain the declared repetitions, sample count, concurrency and warm-up; record revision, resources, source/clip/film dimensions, errors, queue wait, worker and end-to-end time.
5. Keep the runner's local-only URL/credential safeguards. PostgreSQL measurement must use isolated owned fixtures; extending measurement support must not enable arbitrary hosted targets or seed real user data. No new infrastructure or uncontrolled load.

On 12 October the existing retro suite passed 17 tests and film suite passed 6. A temporary real-FFmpeg probe confirmed both 1080p orientations retain their individual-clip dimensions/audio and compile to 720×1280. The benchmark assertion mismatch was separately reproduced. These checks establish the current boundary, not completed benchmark measurements.

title: Repair the film benchmark without changing capture or media quality

body:
## Problem

[The native archive download helper writes only to app cache](https://github.com/Collaboration95/rewind-app/blob/a1dc77e940a824b0d4e9ffaabf1e4ac517e38816/src/archive/archive-download.ts#L103). [Film discards the returned URI and says “Saved.”](https://github.com/Collaboration95/rewind-app/blob/a1dc77e940a824b0d4e9ffaabf1e4ac517e38816/src/real/Film.tsx#L195). There is no share/export step in this path, so an Android member cannot retrieve the purported saved film or own clip through the UI.

#140 established downloading and collision-safe filenames, but app-cache transfer alone does not complete the user-facing download outcome in proposal §4.7. Android remains a hosted-dev test client; this does not add native iOS scope.

## Expected

- After an authorized download, provide a supported Android save/export or share action so the user can access the media outside app-private cache.
- Report completion accurately; cancellation is distinct from successful export and transfer/export failures remain retryable.
- Preserve fresh authorized URLs, filename uniqueness, repeated-tap serialization and owned temporary-file cleanup.
- Do not expose another member's clips or pre-reveal media.

## How to check

Cover transfer failure, export success, user cancellation, unavailable export, repeated taps and cleanup in focused archive/Film tests. Run `npm run test:fast`.

In the rebuilt Android test APK on an emulator or device, save a released film and an own clip, choose a destination, and open both from that destination. Cancel another export and verify no “Saved” claim. Use local/dev developer sign-in; no native push, compiled iOS or app-store work.


## Regression constraints

- Choose an export mechanism supported by the installed Expo SDK. Do not assume legacy copyAsync(fileUri, SAF content:// URI) works; verify the actual native destination path.
- Keep transfer disk-backed. Do not load entire films as JavaScript base64 to implement export.
- Opening/closing a share sheet is not proof that a destination saved the file. Use outcome-appropriate wording; reserve “Saved” for observable successful export.
- Serialize the complete authorize/download/export operation by asset identity, even when repeated taps obtain different signed URLs. Existing URL-keyed transfer coalescing is not sufficient by itself.
- Define cancellation and batch behavior explicitly: cancellation stops remaining own-clip exports, with accurate partial-completion feedback. Do not claim existing transfer cancellation that the helper does not implement.
- Clean only operation-owned temporary/partial files after their consumer is finished. Preserve completed external exports and unrelated cache data.

Test different fresh URLs on repeated taps, partial batch success/cancellation, and real destination access in the APK. Mock success is not proof that an Android user can open the export.

## Problem

[Settings.allow](https://github.com/Collaboration95/rewind-app/blob/a1dc77e940a824b0d4e9ffaabf1e4ac517e38816/src/real/Settings.tsx#L506) stops only for a `denied` enable result. An `error`, `cleanup-pending`, `revoked` snapshot or rejected enable promise still reaches the preference save and “Sunday 7 PM reminders are on for this device” toast. The reminder client distinguishes registration state from the member's scheduling preference.

The UI can therefore claim device delivery is enabled when registration failed. Source inspection confirms this control flow; no live delivery failure is claimed.

## Expected

- Claim this device is enabled only after a confirmed successful device registration.
- Display the returned failure/recovery state or a clear retry message for rejected enable calls.
- Keep scheduling preference separate from device subscription status; do not present saving a preference as registering the device.
- Preserve explicit notification consent and the iPhone Home Screen installation explanation. Avoid duplicate subscriptions on retry.

## How to check

Exercise the current Settings consent dialog with successful registration, denied permission, error, cleanup-pending, revoked state and a rejected enable promise. Verify failure cases never emit the device-enabled success message; retry can reach the successful state; unmount/group switch does not apply stale UI state.

Add focused Settings tests using the existing reminder client contract, then run `npm run test:fast`. Local client tests establish this defect; a remote provider or physical phone is not needed to fix it.


## Regression constraints

- Confirm registration only when the snapshot has state === 'enabled' and enabled === true. This confirms registration, not visible notification delivery.
- Keep group scheduling preferences usable on unsupported/unconfigured devices with truthful preference-only messaging. Handle registration success followed by preference-save failure separately.
- Preserve subscription initiation from the consent gesture, coalesced registration, subscription reuse, per-account association and durable uncertain-registration recovery.
- Preserve group-switch cleanup ordering and immediate sign-out privacy closure. Do not erase recovery metadata, delay logout on network cleanup or let old cleanup remove a newer association. Native push remains paused.

Exercise the current Settings component via tests/real-group-reminders.test.tsx; the older settings-component tests alone do not cover this path. Retain tests/private-reminder-client.test.ts and include stale-result and partial-success scenarios.

body:
## Problem

The initiating client updates a reaction through the HTTP response, but [the reaction route publishes no realtime update](https://github.com/Collaboration95/rewind-app/blob/a1dc77e940a824b0d4e9ffaabf1e4ac517e38816/server/src/http.ts#L1733). Message creation does publish an event. Other members' open chats keep stale counts, and [the client merge preserves existing message rows](https://github.com/Collaboration95/rewind-app/blob/a1dc77e940a824b0d4e9ffaabf1e4ac517e38816/src/chat/RealAccountChatScreen.tsx#L41) instead of reconciling changed reactions on a repeated row.

#50/#252 implemented reactions; this issue covers synchronization of the existing reaction, within the proposal §4.6 real-time private conversation.

## Expected

- Add/remove of the supported reaction reaches other authorized open clients.
- Reconnect reconciles missed reaction changes without duplicating messages, reordering history or incrementing unread-message counts.
- Repeated delivery is idempotent; group/account switches, revoked membership and block visibility keep their existing privacy boundaries.
- Keep the existing reaction and one-level reply scope.

## How to check

Use two members in one group and an outsider. Add/remove a reaction on a message already visible to both; disconnect the second member, change reactions, then reconnect. Assert exact counts/current-member state, no duplicate rows, unchanged unread counts and no outsider/foreign-group event.

Extend `server/tests/chat-replies-reactions.test.mjs` and the relevant client merge/subscription tests. Run focused tests, `npm run test:fast`, and a two-session `make run` check. No typing indicators, read receipts, attachments or new messaging service.


## Regression constraints

- Reaction updates must not masquerade as newly created chat messages. Preserve creation event IDs, ordering, unread counts and the reconnect cursor semantics; use reaction-specific updates/invalidation with a reliable missed-update reconciliation path.
- Patch reaction data safely rather than replacing whole existing rows. Delayed history must not undo newer reactions, and an update must never reinsert reported/hidden content or reveal a redacted quote.
- Preserve composer/reply/failed-send identity, history pagination and scroll. Fence responses after account/group switches.
- Apply existing per-viewer filtering and bidirectional block rules. The mutating caller's reaction.active state is not another viewer's own state and must not be broadcast as such.

Add regressions for out-of-order history/updates, reactions on older paginated messages after reconnect, unchanged unread counts, report/block while an update is in flight, revocation/sign-out and wrong-group denial. Preserve the existing safety tests and avoid weakening authorization to simplify fan-out.

body:
## Problem

[Film requests only one archive page with limit 50](https://github.com/Collaboration95/rewind-app/blob/a1dc77e940a824b0d4e9ffaabf1e4ac517e38816/src/real/Film.tsx#L111) and then filters that page by the viewed cycle. [The server paginates own clips newest-first across all released cycles](https://github.com/Collaboration95/rewind-app/blob/a1dc77e940a824b0d4e9ffaabf1e4ac517e38816/server/src/db.ts#L1985). An older cycle entirely beyond page one loses its save action; a cycle spanning the boundary yields an incomplete download set. Retrieval errors are also swallowed.

This violates the continuing own-clip download outcome in submitted proposal §4.7. #140/#344/#345 delivered the basic download flow; none tracks this pagination defect.

## Expected

- Discover every eligible own clip for the viewed cycle, following the clip cursor or using a bounded cycle-scoped query.
- Save each matching clip once, and no clip from another cycle, group or member.
- Distinguish loading, failure/retry and genuinely having no own clips. Discard results after context changes.
- Preserve current release, membership and fresh-download authorization checks.

## How to check

Extend `tests/film-screen.test.tsx` with more than 50 own clips across released cycles: the selected cycle entirely beyond page one, a cycle split across pages, empty results, retrieval failure/retry and a context change while loading.

Run `npm run test:focused -- frontend tests/film-screen.test.tsx`, then `npm run test:fast`. In a local real-account fixture, open the older film and confirm the exact expected clip IDs are saved once. If the API query changes, add its focused server case. This does not require an archive redesign or bulk-export feature.


## Regression constraints

- Fix clip discovery while retaining getFreshArchiveMedia for each actual download. It already handles paginated authorization and matches both clip and contribution IDs; do not replace it with aging listing URLs.
- Follow the clip cursor independently, deduplicate assets and stop on exhausted or repeated cursors. A failed page must not silently become a partially complete successful save.
- Fence loads by account/client, group, cycle and request generation; an unmount-only alive flag is insufficient for overlapping loads.
- Retrieve metadata only during discovery. Preserve authorized streaming/range handling and serialize media transfers rather than downloading the whole archive into memory.

Retain existing archive-client and real-archive authorization/range tests. Add duplicate/stalled cursor, second-page failure and stale mounted-screen response cases to the Film tests.

body:
## Problem

An open real-account session keeps the initially loaded group/release snapshot and contribution ledger while its displayed clock advances. An exhausted member can stay unable to open capture after the weekly reset; rollover, publication and premiere expiry can remain stale until a reload. This is a current client-state gap, not a missing server scheduler.

Evidence at audited dev `a1dc77e`: [group load and ledger effects](https://github.com/Collaboration95/rewind-app/blob/a1dc77e940a824b0d4e9ffaabf1e4ac517e38816/src/groups/RealAccountGroupExperience.tsx#L477), [clock-derived week using stored allowance/releases](https://github.com/Collaboration95/rewind-app/blob/a1dc77e940a824b0d4e9ffaabf1e4ac517e38816/src/groups/RealAccountGroupExperience.tsx#L883) and the shutter guard in `src/real/Shell.tsx`. Existing #250/#345/#352 cover the basic flow.

## Expected

- Reconcile current cycle, member allowance and release state when the relevant time boundary passes and when the app returns to the foreground.
- Detect a processing film becoming published while the session stays open; use bounded refresh behavior that stops when no longer needed.
- Home, capture eligibility, Chat's premiere banner and Archive agree with server state without a full page reload.
- Ignore stale responses after group/account changes. Failed refreshes retain safe state and offer retry without a request loop.

## How to check

Add focused mounted-client cases in `tests/real-group-experience.test.tsx`: exhausted allowance crossing seven days; cycle rollover; processing-to-published; premiere expiry; foreground return; delayed response after group switching; refresh failure/retry. Use controlled time for long boundaries.

Run `npm run test:focused -- frontend tests/real-group-experience.test.tsx`, then `npm run test:fast`. Exercise one short cycle with `make run-real`, keeping the same browser session open. No scheduler redesign or new physical-device gate is needed.


## Regression constraints

- Refresh quietly without remounting the shell or resetting the selected tab, pushed screen, film selection, chat draft/reply/failed-send state, scroll or Settings inputs.
- Preserve ongoing capture/review/upload ownership and existing interruption rules. Avoid changing callback identity in a way that rehydrates ContributionStatusProvider over a queued/processing/retry state.
- Keep the server authoritative. Retain the last confirmed allowance on a transient failure; clearing it to null can incorrectly make the shutter appear ready. Fence both success and failure by account/group generation and latest request.
- Reconcile an already-open Archive as well as Home releases, preserving its loaded pages. Coalesce requests and keep processing polling bounded.

Add checks for count and seconds exhaustion, cycle-relative weeks, refresh during capture/upload/chat/Settings, stale or overlapping responses, revocation and Archive publication without remounting. Preserve existing capture-close refresh behavior.

**Problem:** Proposal §4.3 says the revealed film "remains permanently accessible from the group archive"; §4.7 allows members to download processed clips after reveal. title: Backup-gated hibernation no longer works after the PostgreSQL cutover

body:
## Problem

The current rollback sets `cutover=false` and returns to the retained pre-cutover SQLite file. Accounts, chat, contributions and other writes made since switching to PostgreSQL are missing after that rollback. `docs/architecture/postgresql-operations.md` records this limitation; the CLI has no reverse-export operation.

## Expected

- Add `node server/dist/cli.js database-export --sqlite PATH` to create a fresh SQLite database at the supported current schema from a consistent PostgreSQL snapshot.
- Preserve types, relationships, application/environment metadata and media references; reconcile every application table by row count and canonical content hash, matching the import guarantees. Validate migration and environment metadata explicitly as well as application-table hashes.
- Reject incompatible schema, inconsistent export, wrong-environment input and an unsafe destination before replacing any live file.
- Quiesce all applicable writers for the final export/switch, including runtime workers, so writes cannot be lost between snapshot and installation.
- Install the validated export using database-only atomic staging/swap and readiness/rollback guarantees. Preserve current disk media and exact S3 object/version references. Do not blindly call the full backup restore: `deploy/restore.sh` also swaps the media tree and could replace current media with an older snapshot. Keep the prior target and PostgreSQL recoverable if validation, swap or startup fails.
- A lossless reverse export requires readable PostgreSQL. If the source is unavailable, use the documented managed/logical-backup recovery path and report its actual recovery point; do not claim zero loss.
- Update rollback guidance to distinguish a proven lossless export from intentionally returning to an old snapshot.

## How to check

Use isolated PostgreSQL/SQLite fixtures: import a snapshot, create post-cutover account/group/chat/contribution and job changes, export, and compare every table's rows/count/hash. Include nulls, booleans, timestamps and identifiers supported by the schema.

Open the result with SQLite and verify sign-in/session handling, the new chat/contribution, owned media references and environment binding. Test interrupted export, reconciliation failure, wrong environment, existing destination and failed install/startup; none may destroy a valid database or silently drop writes.

Run focused database tests and test:fast. Complete one isolated end-to-end rollback rehearsal preserving known post-cutover writes and media via the documented writer-stop/export/switch procedure. Use disposable databases/media; do not require switching the live hosted-dev database back merely to close this issue. #504 reuses this recovery path. No source database deletion is required.

body:
## Problem

The release configuration still disables managed PostgreSQL (`release.enabled=false`, `cutover=false` in `infra/terraform/media/database.tf`) and sets `backup_prefix_arn=null` in `infra/terraform/release/main.tf`. The database operations workflow hard-codes dev role, host, database, environment and concurrency. Dev's delivered database and recovery results do not establish release recovery.

This describes repository configuration; #230 tracks completion of the first release application deployment.

## Expected

- Provision/bind a separate release PostgreSQL database and generated roles using existing per-environment configuration.
- Provide release-only managed backups plus the existing restore-verified logical backup route, with isolated storage permissions and the actual host backup settings/timer. Release must have explicit bucket/prefix/settings, with no fallback to dev defaults. Preserve verified TLS, private release database access, environment binding, destruction protection and final snapshots.
- Make bootstrap/import/status/backup/restore operations explicitly target release through release-appropriate workflow protection, identity, host, configuration and concurrency. Refuse ambiguous or cross-environment operations.
- Before the final SQLite snapshot, stop/drain all writers, including the runtime scheduler, reminder loop and media workers. Keep them stopped through snapshot, reconciled import and cutover; stopping only the web proxy is insufficient. Resume only the selected authoritative database after health validation.
- Import retained release data with per-table count/content reconciliation, then switch to PostgreSQL through the normal reviewed deployment.
- Preserve data and media references. Use #505 for a lossless post-cutover SQLite rollback; an old SQLite snapshot must not be described as lossless.

## How to check

1. Relevant configuration/operation fixtures reject wrong environment/host/role combinations. A release Terraform plan changes only the intended release resources.
2. After reviewed setup/cutover, release health reports `checks.database: "postgresql"`; status reports release binding and current schema. Dev remains healthy.
3. Verify release data survives restart; a dev runtime pointed at release refuses startup, and dev identities cannot read release backups.
4. Run the release backup and restore rehearsal using an isolated restore target. Reconcile tables and record actual recovery-point age and time to a usable restored database, without inventing an RPO/RTO promise.
5. Test that a due scheduler/reminder/media operation cannot write to the old database after the final snapshot. Exercise interrupted import/cutover and the documented recovery path on owned fixtures; source data stays intact.

Run focused server/operation checks and test:fast for changes. This completes the existing release outcome under #230; no standby, new environment or broader availability architecture is required.

title: Move the release environment onto managed PostgreSQL with isolated backups

body:
## Problem

The hosted database runs on a single Lightsail PostgreSQL instance in one availability zone (`micro_2_0`). If that instance or its zone fails, the app is down until someone restores a backup. The PostgreSQL work (#261) gives the app a reconnect path and a backup-based recovery, but no standby to fail over to.

## Expected

- The hosted database runs on a high-availability bundle (`micro_ha_2_0`, US$30/month instead of US$15). This adds a standby in a second availability zone with automatic failover behind the same endpoint. The switch is `bundle` in `local.database_settings` (`infra/terraform/media/database.tf`).
- During a failover the app recovers without manual action:
  - a dropped connection is replaced on the next statement;
  - an in-flight transaction fails once and rolls back;
  - `/health` reports unavailable until the database answers again.
- The measured interruption is recorded in the runbook (`docs/architecture/postgresql-operations.md` → Failover).

## How to check

- Apply with the HA bundle. `aws lightsail get-relational-database` shows the HA bundle and a secondary availability zone.
- Reboot the database (`aws lightsail reboot-relational-database`) while the hosted app is in use. Chat and the group screen work again within the measured window with no manual step, and no request reports partial data.
- `server/tests/postgres.test.mjs` "a dropped connection … reconnects" passes in Quality.

**Problem:** `deploy-dev.yml` triggers on every push to `dev`, runs its own `changes` classification, then in the `deploy` job polls the GitHub API every 20 seconds for up to 25 minutes (`Wait for this commit's dev Quality checks`) until `quality.yml` succeeds. body:
**Problem:** Quality repeats setup work in every job:
- `npm ci` runs in five jobs (`static`, `server`, `frontend`, `browser`, `fixtures`), and `fixtures` only runs bash scripts that may not need it.
- `server:build` runs in both `static` (via `test:root`) and `server`.
- Playwright Chromium (`npx playwright install --with-deps chromium`) is downloaded on every `static` run and is not cached, although only the root HTTP integration tests need it.
- `ffmpeg` is installed by `apt-get update && install` in three jobs.
- The `changes` jobs in `quality.yml` and `deploy-dev.yml` use `fetch-depth: 0` (full history) just to diff two SHAs.

**Expected:** Remove or share what is safe: cache `~/.cache/ms-playwright` keyed on the Playwright version; confirm which root tests actually need Playwright and move the install to the job that runs them; drop `npm ci` from `fixtures` if the scripts do not use `node_modules`; use a shallow checkout and fetch only the base SHA in the `changes` jobs. Behaviour and test coverage are unchanged.

**How to check:** Compare the step durations in a PR run against the baseline issue. Confirm cache hit on a second run. `fixtures`, `static` and `server` still pass; run `classify-quality-changes.mjs` against a shallow clone and confirm identical output to the full-history run for a docs-only and a code change.

Do not share `server/dist` through artifacts unless the saving is measurable; the extra upload and download can cost more than `tsc`.

Part of #481. Read the parent's **Agent brief** first.

## Problem
1. **Lockout looks like a wrong password.** After 5 failed attempts the account cools down for 15 minutes or longer (`server/src/auth/index.ts`, throttle/cooldown). But the throttled result returns the same `401 sign_in_failed` as a wrong password (`server/src/http.ts`, `/auth/login`). The client then shows "Wrong username or password." (`App.tsx`), so users keep retyping a correct password.
2. **Server errors say "offline".** `noticeFor` in `src/auth/RealAccountProvider.tsx` maps every non-401 failure (including 5xx and 502) to `'offline'`, which shows "You're offline. Sign in again when you're connected." Session restore does the same.
3. **Registering makes you sign in again.** On `'created'`, the password fields are cleared and the user is sent to sign-in with "Your account is ready. Sign in to continue."

## Expected
1. When throttled, return `429` with `Retry-After`, keeping the same response for known and unknown usernames. The client shows "Too many attempts. Try again in about N minutes." (rounded from `Retry-After`).
2. `status >= 500` (and non-JSON gateway pages) shows "Rewind is having trouble right now. Try again in a minute." A real network failure still shows offline.
3. After `'created'`, sign in automatically with the same credentials. If that fails, fall back to today's message. Keep the invite-acceptance flow working.
4. An optional `revealable` prop on `Field` with an eye button (`accessibilityLabel` "Show password" / "Hide password"), used on the sign-in, register and delete-account password fields.

## How to check
- Focused server test: 6 wrong attempts gives 429 with `Retry-After`, and an unknown username gets the same response.
- Focused client tests for `noticeFor` and the register flow.
- `make run-real`: lock yourself out and read the message, register a new account and land signed in, toggle the password visibility.

## Problem

Small rough edges make the real-account app feel less finished than it is. Each one below is confirmed in `origin/dev` (6 Oct 2026). Each is under half a day, and none needs a new dependency, endpoint or architecture change.

## Expected

The sub-issues are fixed in **one branch and one PR**. Every message a user can see is plain, accurate and actionable, with no raw error codes, browser exception text or developer jargon.

## How to check

`npm run test:fast`, plus `npm run web` / `make run-real` for each item's own check (listed in each sub-issue).

---

## Agent brief (use as the prompt)

**Goal:** polish, not features. Prefer editing existing copy and helpers over adding new modules. Each fix should be a few lines.

**Read first:** `AGENTS.md`, `skills/ship-issues/SKILL.md`, this issue and each sub-issue. Line numbers are from `origin/dev` @ 19b9263 and may have drifted, so search by the quoted text.

**Order:** sub-issue A (sign-in and registration), then B (error copy), then C (chat, invites, archive). They touch different files, so lanes can run in parallel worktrees and be integrated into one PR.

**Constraints**

- **No user enumeration.** Never return a message that reveals whether a username exists. The throttle covers unknown usernames too, so a "too many attempts" (429) response is safe. A per-account "locked" message is not.
- Do not touch the frozen Demo screens (`src/archive/ArchiveScreen.tsx` and other Demo-only code; see AGENTS.md). The real Archive is `src/real/Archive.tsx`.
- Keep assertions. Update a test's expected copy only where the copy itself is the fix.
- Two-attempt diagnosis rule.
- Review: A touches sign-in, so run the sensitive review (`gpt-6.1-sol`, medium). Otherwise use Luna.

**Running it with Codex** (codex-cli 0.160.0; this command was tested on this Mac):

```sh
codex exec -m gpt-6-luna -c model_reasoning_effort="high" -c service_tier="fast" -c features.fast_mode=true \
  -s workspace-write -C /path/to/lane-worktree -o /tmp/luna-<sub>.md \
  "Implement sub-issue #<n> of #<parent>. Read the parent's Agent brief via gh first."
codex exec review --base origin/dev -m gpt-6.1-sol -c model_reasoning_effort="medium"
```

## Deliberately not included

- **"Forgot password?" link.** Waits on the owner choosing a support contact (accounts have no email, so there is no self-serve reset).
- **Leave group / hand over ownership, self-serve password reset, live "username available" check, phone-number sign-up.** Each needs new endpoints, rules or a recovery channel. Not quick wins.
- **Password-strength library (zxcvbn).** The 12-character rule is already shown up front.
- **Already good, so leave alone:** password-manager autofill attributes, username-taken message, empty and retry states, delete confirmations, chat retry, upload progress, accessibility labels.

Part of #475. Read the parent's **Agent brief** first. Depends on sub-issue 1.

## Problem
`verifiedServingPath` and `verifiedArchiveListingPath` (`server/src/http.ts`) call `verifyReadyJobOutput`, which re-reads the whole S3 object (or re-hashes the disk file) on every Archive listing, premiere-status check and download grant.

## Expected
- Listing, premiere status and the download grant use one cheap check: the job row is `ready`, has a digest, size and `output_verified_at`, and its path is not an `incoming` ref. For S3, a single `store.head()` is acceptable if it fits naturally. Disk may use one `stat`.
- Bytes are hashed only when streamed (`openStoredServingFile` / `openVerifiedServingFile`, unchanged).
- Tests asserting "corrupt media is hidden from the Archive list" are rewritten to the new contract: listed, fails safely on play, audited. That contract is covered by sub-issue 1.

## How to check
- Focused tests: `real-archive`, `media-integrity`, `private-media-jobs`, `paging-performance`. Then `npm run test:fast`.
- `make run-real`: Archive lists released media, playing and downloading work, and a corrupted file fails on play with an audit event.

body:

title: Prove playback alone rejects corrupted disk and S3 media

body:
## Problem

On hosted (S3 media), every Archive view, premiere-status check and download
pre-check reads each listed film and clip **back from S3 in full** to re-hash it
before the server will list or offer it. Nothing caches the result for S3:

- `GET /archive` → `filterServableArchive` → `verifiedArchiveListingPath` →
  `verifyReadyJobOutput` (`server/src/jobs/index.ts`) → `verifyStoredMedia`
  (`server/src/media/store.ts`), which does a HEAD and then streams the whole
  object only to throw the bytes away.
- Premiere status (`verifiedServingPath`) and the download grant (`verifiedServingPath`
  in the download route) do the same.
- Local disk media re-hashes the file too. The Archive listing alone has an
  in-memory cache (`server/src/archive/integrity-cache.ts`, 139 lines) that
  exists only to soften this cost.

Playback already checks the bytes when it actually streams them:
`server/src/archive/store-serving.ts` materialises the object, hashes it
(`openMediaWithIntegrity`), and on mismatch records an audit event
(`recordIntegrityFailure`) and refuses to serve. So the checks at list time
repeat work that playback does anyway, cost S3 bandwidth and memory on a
1 GB VM, and need extra code (the cache) to stay tolerable.

## Expected

Listing, premiere status and the download grant decide from the database row
alone (`status = 'ready'`, digest, size and `output_verified_at` present, not an
`incoming` ref). For S3, one `HEAD` to confirm the object still exists is
acceptable if it is cheap and already available. Bytes are hashed **once**, when
they are streamed. Net code goes **down**: the integrity cache and the
listing-specific helper are deleted.

**Accepted behaviour change (owner accepted on 6 Oct 2026):** a file
corrupted *after* processing could appear in the Archive list and then fail on
play with the existing safe "unavailable" response and audit event, instead of
being hidden from the list. Playback integrity, the audit trail and refusal to
serve bad bytes are unchanged.

## How to check

- `npm run test:focused -- server server/tests/real-archive.test.mjs` (plus the
  media-integrity and paging tests touched) and then `npm run test:fast`.
- `make run-real`: release a cycle, open Archive, play a film and download a
  clip. Then corrupt a stored processed file on disk and confirm that playing it
  returns the safe unavailable response and writes an integrity audit event.
- Hosted dev after deploy: open Archive with a few films. The S3 GET count from the
  runtime should no longer grow with every Archive refresh (only on play or
  download).

---

## Agent brief (use as the prompt)

**Goal:** delete duplicate media verification. Do not add a new layer. This is a
simplification issue: the best PR removes more lines than it adds.

**Read first:** `AGENTS.md`, `skills/ship-issues/SKILL.md`, this issue and its
sub-issues. Then read these files in full: `server/src/http.ts` (functions
`verifiedServingPath`, `verifiedArchiveListingPath`, `filterServableArchive`,
the premiere route and the download route), `server/src/jobs/index.ts`
(`verifyReadyJobOutput`), `server/src/media/store.ts` (`verifyStoredMedia`),
`server/src/archive/store-serving.ts`, `server/src/archive/integrity-cache.ts`.

**Order:** do the sub-issues in order, as **one branch and one PR** (CLAUDE.md
"one PR per batch").

1. Prove that the stream-time check catches corruption for both disk and S3 (a test).
2. Replace the three pre-checks with one cheap state check.
3. Delete the dead code (integrity cache, listing helper, unused exports).

**Constraints**

- Keep `uploadIntents`/finalisation and film-publication verification
  (`publishCompilationOutput`, `verifyStoredMedia` at publish time) unchanged.
  Hashing once when the output is *written* is correct. Only the repeated
  *read-time* checks go.
- Never remove an assertion that still describes current behaviour. Tests for
  deleted code are deleted with that code. Tests that assert "corrupt media is
  hidden from the listing" are rewritten to assert "corrupt media fails safely
  on play and is audited".
- Two-attempt rule for diagnosis (AGENTS.md).
- Review: private media is sensitive, so run the GPT-6.1 Sol medium review (below).

**Running it with Codex** (codex-cli 0.160.0; this command was tested on this Mac):

```sh
# Implementation worker: Luna, fast tier, inside its own worktree
codex exec \
  -m gpt-6-luna \
  -c model_reasoning_effort="high" \
  -c service_tier="fast" \
  -c features.fast_mode=true \
  -s workspace-write \
  -C /path/to/worktree \
  -o /tmp/luna-<issue>.md \
  "Implement sub-issue #<n> of #<parent> in this worktree. Read the parent issue's Agent brief via gh first."

# Required review before merge (private media is sensitive)
codex exec review --base origin/dev -m gpt-6.1-sol -c model_reasoning_effort="medium"
```

- `service_tier` accepts `"fast"`, `"priority"` or `"default"`. CLAUDE.md uses
  `"priority"` for its Luna review. Either works; the run fails fast if the account
  lacks the tier.
- `features.fast_mode=true` is already the default in this Mac's
  `~/.codex/config.toml`. Passing it explicitly is harmless.
- `-o` writes the worker's final message to a file the orchestrator can read.
  Use `--json` for event streams.
- Harmless startup warnings on this Mac: "malformed agent role `worker`", a
  claude-dashboard hooks parse warning, and a websocket 426 that falls back to HTTP.

---

## Considered and rejected (do not re-propose without a measured problem)

From a code review plus micro-benchmarks on 6 Oct 2026. Each of these would add
code or moving parts for a gain under a millisecond per request at ~10 users:

- **Statement cache** for the ~374 inline `prepare()` calls: saves 2–8 µs per
  query and adds a shared cache across ~32 files. No.
- **Throttling the `last_seen_at` write** in `validateRealSession`: adds
  time-based branching to auth. No.
- **`PRAGMA synchronous=NORMAL`**: a durability trade-off in `db.ts` with no
  measured problem. No.
- **Removing the "duplicate" auth checks** in the media and chat routes: they
  re-validate identity after an `await`, so revocation and removal take effect
  mid-request. That is deliberate. Keep them.
- **Chat stream re-auth on every event or heartbeat**: deliberate revocation
  behaviour. Keep it.
- **Caching `schemaReadiness` for `/health`, or slowing the 1 s scheduler**:
  adds state or tuning for about 1 ms every 30 s. No.

body:
## Problem

After successful deployment of dev `0ea1b0d`, the hosted synthetic Demo reaches Warm Glass Home, Moments, Chat, Archive and Settings, but its existing owner reveal control returns `delayed`. The panel says “The film is delayed. No player or download has been published.” The hosted end-to-end Film/replay check cannot continue.

Two bounded diagnoses reproduced the failure. The second waits for the control to finish rather than relying on a short delay; all observed responses remain delayed. There are no uncaught browser page errors. The same final source releases, decodes and replays its Film successfully in the local production runtime. The reveal-control logic existed in the baseline; causality is unproven. Do not add Demo features.

## Expected

The hosted Demo's existing reveal path compiles and publishes its Film, or exposes a useful existing error so the underlying runtime failure can be corrected.

## How to check

1. Open https://d2m6kz76y4kuvm.cloudfront.net without a real account, choose Try Demo and the existing owner persona.
2. Open Settings, use the existing local reveal control, and wait for the action to finish.
3. Confirm release rather than repeated delayed state; open Archive, play the actual encoded Film, reach Film end and use Replay, with no uncaught page errors.

Found during the final phase of PR #465; current hosted health is ready at migration 30 and security headers pass. Diagnostic JSON and screenshot are retained in the overnight report's local evidence folder. No hosted real accounts were created.

body:
## Problem

The final merged-dev production export rejects tests/fixtures/portrait-h264-aac.mp4 when selected in desktop Playwright WebKit from a local real-account video capture screen. The visible error is “Choose an MP4 video that includes an audio track readable by the server.” Review never opens; no uncaught page error occurs.

FFprobe confirms720×1280 H.264 High plus AAC LC, approximately2.27seconds. Two bounded file-import attempts (path payload and explicit video/mp4 buffer payload) reproduce the rejection. The MP4 sound-track guard and loadedmetadata audioTracks predicate already existed in the baseline; causality is not established. No assertion was weakened. Actual injected WebKit recording and released Film playback pass separately. Chromium's15-second H.264/AAC real Blob/disk upload seals successfully.

## Expected

A valid supported MP4 containing video and an AAC sound track opens truthful file-labelled review in WebKit and can be submitted for authoritative server verification. Unknown or incomplete browser audio hints must not be confused with proven missing audio. Keep real rejection of files without audio and retain server-side verification.

## How to check

Use the production export over local HTTPS with a disposable real account, open Video's file fallback and choose the fixture above in WebKit. Inspect container metadata, loadedmetadata audio hints and decoder readiness; compare with the baseline before attributing a regression. Verify play/pause and real sealing. Preserve existing sound-track rejection assertions and run focused browser/platform tests, npm run test:fast and required web slow/a11y checks.

**Problem**

The web live look uses the shared RETRO_LOOKS filters, tint, vignette and grain, but its CSS approximation does not yet match all grading applied to the sealed photo. In a 402×874 Chromium real-account check with a static synthetic white/orange camera, UI scrims hidden only during pixel sampling, the live preview was compared with a decoded frame of the actual sealed local photo at the same center-cover size. Mean absolute RGB channel differences on a 0–255 scale were:

- Disposable Flash: 17.49 / 19.26 / 21.21
- Compact Digital: 6.02 / 6.24 / 6.42
- 8mm Home Movie: 19.01 / 19.07 / 19.16
- VHS Camcorder: 22.97 / 22.31 / 21.79

Only Compact Digital meets the requested ≤8 per-channel threshold. Shared spec mapping tests pass for all four looks. CSS preview lacks some final canvas effects and its vignette/grain geometry differs. This is a fidelity gap, rather than missing live look selection. Follow-up from #460 under the overnight plan's measured-gap fallback.

**Expected**

All four live previews and reviews match the corresponding sealed photo grading within a mean absolute difference of 8/255 per RGB channel on a deterministic camera fixture. Preserve reduced-motion support and usable recording performance.

**How to check**

At 402×874, use a static fake camera, select each look, capture the clean live media layer, take and seal a photo through the real-account flow, then decode the retained sealed photo frame. Normalize both images to the same displayed crop and compare RGB channels. Retain the ≤8 threshold and run the existing RETRO_LOOKS mapping tests, capture checks, test:fast, slow and accessibility suites. Verify the PWA preview on Safari.

body:
**Problem**

`member_reports.reported_account_id` and the `content_reports` content columns cascade on delete (`server/migrations/028`, `029`), so an abuser who deletes their account erases every report against them. The FK columns used by those cascades and lookups have no indexes (`content_reports(message_id|contribution_id|group_id)`, `account_blocks(blocked_account_id)`, `member_reports(reported_account_id|group_id)`, `film_segments(contribution_id)`, `contributions(removed_by_account_id)`), so deletes scan whole tables.

**Expected**

Reports survive deletion of the reported account or content (`ON DELETE SET NULL`, keeping reason, reporter and time). A new migration adds the indexes.

**How to check**

Server test: report a member, delete their account, the report row remains with a null target. `EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN` for the cascade lookups uses the new indexes.

body:
Parent: #427

**Problem:** Real-account sessions use an HttpOnly cookie (`Secure; SameSite=Lax`). Cookie handling in React Native `fetch` on iOS is less predictable than in a browser: cookies may not persist across app restarts, and a cross-origin API host can break them. This risks reviewers getting signed out or failing to sign in.

**Expected:** The native iOS build keeps a session reliably across app restarts. One way: when the native client signs in, the server also returns the session token. The client stores it in `expo-secure-store` (already installed) and sends it as an `Authorization: Bearer` header. The web client keeps the HttpOnly cookie. Never store the token in AsyncStorage.

**How to check:** On an iPhone simulator (Expo dev build, not Expo Go if cookies differ), sign in, kill the app and reopen it. The user is still signed in, and sign-out revokes the session on the server. Add a focused server test for bearer-token authentication.

Parent: #427

**Problem:** Group members share photos and videos, which makes them user-generated content. App Store Guideline 1.2 requires apps with user-generated content to provide:
- a way to filter or remove objectionable material
- a way to report offensive content, with timely responses
- a way to block abusive users
- published contact information

Rewind has none of these today.

**Expected:**
- **Report:** a user can report a moment from the moment view, with an optional reason. The server stores the report and hides the moment from the reporter right away. Operators can list reports (a CLI command or an admin query is enough).
- **Block:** a user can block another member. Blocked members' moments are hidden from the blocker, and they can no longer interact with the blocker.
- **Remove:** a contributor can delete their own moment, and the group owner can remove any moment in the group.
- Support contact details appear in the app (see the privacy policy and support URL sub-issue).

**How to check:**
1. Run `make run-real` with two accounts in one group.
2. Report a moment and confirm it is hidden for the reporter and stored on the server.
3. Block the other user and confirm their moments are hidden.
4. As the group owner, remove a moment.
5. Add focused server tests for the report and block routes.

body:
Parent: #427

**Problem:** Users can create a real account in the app but cannot delete it. App Store Guideline 5.1.1(v) requires in-app account deletion for any app that supports account creation, and it is the most common rejection reason. The server has no delete-account route, and the client has no delete control.

**Expected:**
- **Server:** an authenticated route deletes the signed-in `real_accounts` row after the user confirms their password. The deletion must:
  - revoke all of the account's sessions (`real_account_sessions` already uses `ON DELETE CASCADE`)
  - remove or anonymise the account's group memberships, contributions and stored media (on disk locally, on S3 when hosted) through the existing retention or job paths
  - leave other members' content intact
- **Client:** a "Delete account" control in account settings with a clear, irreversible confirmation step. After deletion, the app returns to the sign-in screen.
- Deletion must not need an email, a support ticket or a website visit. Apple rejects those flows.

**How to check:**
1. Run `make run-real` and create an account.
2. Join a group and post a moment.
3. Delete the account from settings, then confirm all of these:
   - signing in again fails
   - the session cookie is rejected
   - the deleted user's media is gone
   - other members still see their own moments
4. Add a focused server test for the delete route.

The app is already Expo / React Native, so the work is an EAS build, App Store Connect setup, and the features Apple requires. It is not a rewrite.

**Expected:** Rewind passes App Review and is available on the App Store (or at least on TestFlight).

**How to check:** App Store Connect shows the build as "Ready for Distribution" (or TestFlight external testing is approved).

## Context

**Authentication:** Apple does not require OIDC. The current username and password sign-in (scrypt, HttpOnly + Secure + SameSite cookies, login throttling, registration rate limit) is acceptable. Sign in with Apple (Guideline 4.8) is **not** required, because we offer no third-party or social login.

**Timelines:**

| Step | Typical time |
| --- | --- |
| Developer Program, individual ($99/yr) | 1–2 days |
| Developer Program, organisation (D-U-N-S) | 1–3 weeks |
| TestFlight, internal | No review |
| TestFlight, external | Beta review, < 1 day |
| App Store review | ~90% decided in < 24 h |
| First submission, realistic | 1–2 weeks with one or two rejections |

**Reminders:** reminders are web push only, and Expo push is turned off. The native build has no reminders unless native push is turned back on. That is a separate decision and is not part of this issue.

## Steps (sub-issues, in order)

1. Enrol in the Apple Developer Program. Start now; it's the longest wait.
2. In-app account deletion (blocker, 5.1.1(v))
3. Report, block and remove controls for shared content (blocker, 1.2)
4. Privacy policy and support URL (blocker, 5.1.1 / 1.5)
5. Permission purpose strings and export compliance flag
6. Reliable native session auth on iOS
7. EAS build and TestFlight internal
8. Reviewer demo account on a stable backend (2.1)
9. App Store Connect listing and submission

body:
Observed during #252 verification on accepted dev `fc2b8c811e9c13b176113fa0bdb2c015798990b4`, iPhone 17 Pro / iOS 26.5, Expo Go 57.0.9 over LAN, with API base `https://d2m6kz76y4kuvm.cloudfront.net/api`.

A real joined second member opens Chat. History, owner/member names, reply context and the event stream load correctly; the UI reports Connected. Select Reply on the existing owner message, enter a labelled acceptance reply, and press Send message. The composer retains the draft and reports “The requested resource was not found.” The native reply was not accepted. The same group's authenticated API text/reply/reaction operations passed in the bounded hosted check, so do not classify API success as UI send acceptance.

Likely cause from source inspection: `RealtimeChatClient` builds a URL including the `/api` base path; `RealAccountChatScreen` passes its full pathname to `authenticatedRequest`, whose real-account client appends the API base path again. This can produce `/api/api/realtime/...` for writes. History calls use an API-relative path directly and the SSE client uses its full URL directly, explaining why reads/connectivity work. This is an inference from the code and observed error, not a captured native network trace.

Expected outcome: iOS native and Home Screen clients send text/replies and toggle reactions through the intended API route when the base has a path prefix, retaining authorization and idempotent retry. Cover the composed client adapter with a path-prefixed base, including reads, writes and reconnect.

Related to #252 and #352. File separately and defer implementation per the owner's current instruction. No application code was changed for this bug.

body:
**Problem.** Rewind verifies passwords itself on every environment. The submitted project document (§4.1, §5.2, §6, §7.1) requires standards-based OIDC sign-in with Amazon Cognito User Pools preferred, and no password storage on release.

**Expected.**
- One Cognito user pool per environment (dev, release) from one Terraform module: email + password, email verified, self sign-up, no MFA, Essentials tier, default prefix domain, Managed Login branded in Warm Glass colours.
- The server does the authorization-code + PKCE exchange (`/api/auth/cognito/start`, `/api/auth/callback`), validates the ID token (issuer, audience, expiry, signature, nonce, state, replayed state) and issues the existing opaque Rewind session. `cognito_sub` links the account (new migration, SQLite + PostgreSQL).
- Rewind session idle expiry 7 days. Sign-out also ends the Cognito session. Account deletion calls `AdminDeleteUser` (runtime IAM scoped to the pool), then the existing purge.
- `REWIND_AUTH_PASSWORD` keeps password sign-in for local runs, tests and hosted dev; release refuses to start with it on.

**How to check.** `server/tests/cognito-auth.test.mjs` (offline, generated RSA key and preloaded JWKS); `npm run test:fast`; on hosted dev the Managed Login page loads with the branding and a Developer sign-in account completes create group → invite → join.

Decisions: `doc/planning/sprints/sprint-3-cognito/prompt.md`.

### Outcome
Provide a small, exact-file local feedback command and bounded guidance that shorten diagnosis while preserving the existing delivery gates.

### Scope and exclusions
- Add an allowlisted selector for one frontend Jest file, one server Node test, or one root Node/shell test. Reject unknown suites, malformed selectors, and paths outside the supported test roots; preserve the selected command's failure exit status.

- Do not alter product/server behavior, introduce a test framework or dependency, or weaken `test:fast`, `test:slow`, frontend/server coverage, `check`, CI Quality, review, or acceptance requirements. A focused pass is only local diagnosis evidence.

### Prerequisites and ownership
No code prerequisite. Work is isolated on `guru/s2-tooling-2026-10-02` from `450a7199767ecc4ea3e96f0f7503d0f2170d382c`. This lane owns ports 5431–5439 and its temporary data/processes; it must not terminate unrelated processes. No changes to product/server domains, HTTP, migrations, configuration, or `RealAccountGroupExperience`.

1. Record one representative focused UI run, one focused server run, and `npm run test:fast`, including exact commands, exit codes, elapsed times, commit/tree state, and Node/npm/platform metadata. Report observed timings only; do not claim a speedup without comparable measurements.
2. Exact selection invokes only the named test file with its existing runner. Unknown selectors and unsupported paths fail clearly. A failing selected test returns a nonzero result to the caller.
3. Runner tests exercise valid selector mapping, invalid selector/path handling, and child failure exit propagation.
4. Shared guidance gives exact commands and bounded retries, preserves fast/slow/coverage/CI and sensitive human review, and leaves cleanup to owned resources.
5. Keep implementation within the 3–6 hour estimate; stop wrapper expansion if measurements show insufficient payback.

### Boundaries
`package.json`; `scripts/**`; `skills/agent-solve-issue/SKILL.md`; runner tests; narrowly scoped, explicit `AGENTS.md` guidance. Dependency and lockfile edits belong to this lane if evidence makes them necessary; none is presumed.

body:
## Priority

**Critical (P0):** Users cannot verify a video contribution before submitting it.

## Problem

After recording and choosing **Stop and review**, the user reports that there is no playable preview of the captured video. They cannot confirm the content, framing, or audio before upload.

The provided screenshot shows the capture screen back at **Start recording** with the message “The browser recording must be portrait video. Turn your phone upright and try again.” The failed capture never reached review. Independently, successful captures also have no playback UI in the review state.

## Code path

- `src/capture/platform.ts` (`recordBrowserClip`) rejects browser recordings whose measured width is greater than or equal to height, with the portrait-orientation message. It releases the camera stream before the error is shown.
- `src/capture/VideoCaptureScreen.tsx` renders review after `replaceClip(recorded)` succeeds. The panel shows metadata, trim fields, and actions, but does not render a player for `clip.sourceUri`.

## Expected behavior

- A successfully recorded clip is playable in review before upload.
- Playback controls allow the user to play and pause, and seek when supported.
- Retake and upload remain available from review.
- When a capture is rejected for orientation, explain the failure and let the user recover without an empty-looking camera view.
- Verify on a physical iPhone using the same Demo/browser recording path.

body:
## Priority

**Critical (P0):** A user cannot see what they are recording, making video capture unusable.

## Problem

When signed into the Demo account and starting a video contribution, the camera preview disappears as soon as recording starts. The attached screenshot shows the recording UI without a visible live camera image, so the user cannot frame or monitor the contribution.

## Code path

In `src/capture/VideoCaptureScreen.tsx`, the live `CameraView` is rendered only when `access === "ready" && !clip && !recording`. - Starting a video contribution keeps the live camera preview visible while recording.

body:
## User outcome

When the team compares performance before and after a change, it can get stable, repeatable numbers without attaching a profiler every time:

- **Server:** per-endpoint latency (p50/p95).
- **Client:** duration of key steps such as "tap to usable screen".

These numbers feed directly into the pivot table and dot plot defined in #267. No identity, content, or secret is recorded.

## Rationale

`dev` currently has **no request-level timing data**.

- **Server:** only audit events (`server/src/audit`: session and job start/complete/fail, ISO-8601 millisecond timestamps) and CLI output exist.
  - Job execution time can already be derived from `job.started` and `job.completed`, which `runAuditedJob` writes.
  - Ordinary HTTP endpoints (Home data, Archive, chat, sign-in) record no latency at all.
- **Client:** there are no performance marks. End points such as "tab switched and Home data rendered" are hard for external tools to observe precisely, so today they are estimated from screenshots.

External tools cover part of this:

| Need | Without code changes | Gap |
|---|---|---|
| Endpoint latency | autocannon | One endpoint at a time; no per-endpoint timing inside a real journey |
| Finding hotspots | `--cpu-prof`, DevTools | High overhead; diagnosis only |
| Web visual comparison | sitespeed.io video | Measures pixels appearing, not data being usable |
| Native tap to usable | Manual DevTools or video review | Not repeatable |

The change can be small:

- **Server:** every request passes through `createRuntimeServer` in `server/src/http.ts`, so timing needs only one entry point.
- **Client:** only a few marks are needed.
- **No new dependency:** `performance.mark` and `performance.measure` are the standard User Timing API. React Native DevTools (Performance panel, RN ≥ 0.83), Chrome DevTools, and sitespeed.io all read them.
- **Not a second logging system:** a full logging pipeline (structured logs, CloudWatch shipping, alarms) remains #166's scope.

## Decision gate

This is a conditional proposal, not an instruction to implement. Proceed only when all of the following hold:

1. The #267 recommendation has been accepted.
2. Round-1 journeys are chosen, and at least one required start or end boundary cannot be observed reliably with external tools.
3. The owner agrees that the fields and redaction rules align with #166, or decides to fold this proposal into #166.

If sitespeed.io and autocannon suffice for round 1, this proposal may be deferred or closed without implementation.

This issue alone authorizes no hosted logging change and no AWS change.

## Scope if the gate passes

- **Server request timing (off by default):**
  - Measure each request in `createRuntimeServer`, from receipt until the response `finish` event, with a monotonic clock.
  - Emit one JSON line per request with fields aligned to OpenTelemetry HTTP conventions:
    - an event name, for example `"event":"http_timing"`, so these lines can be filtered from existing console output;
    - `http.request.method`;
    - `http.route`: a **normalized route template**, for example `/groups/:id`, `/clips/:id`, `/archive`. The runtime has no router table, so this needs a small ordered path-to-template normalizer. Unmatched paths are logged as `other`, never raw.
    - `http.response.status_code`;
    - `duration_ms`;
    - timestamp.
  - Tag streaming media responses and exclude long-lived realtime event streams (`/realtime/groups/:id/events`), because their duration reflects transfer or connection lifetime, not processing.
  - Enable it with an environment variable parsed in `server/src/config.ts` (for example `REWIND_TIMING_LOG=1`) and document the variable. Hosted environments leave it off unless #166 decides otherwise.
- **Job timing:** add a small script or CLI option that exports, from existing audit events and job rows:
  - job execution time (`job.started` → `job.completed`);
  - queue wait (job `created_at` → `job.started`).
  - No new audit event types.
- **Client User Timing:**
  - Add `performance.mark` and `performance.measure` at the start and end of J1 (cold launch to Home), J2 (tab switch), and J3 (Archive paging), through one small helper.
  - Enable it with a build-time flag (for example `EXPO_PUBLIC_PERF_MARKS=1`), **not** with `__DEV__`, so marks also work in the production-mode builds used for formal comparisons.
  - Marks carry names only, never data.
  - Confirm availability on Hermes (Expo SDK 57 / RN 0.86) for iOS and Android, and on web.
- **Privacy:** follow the audit module's rules (`safeAuditIdentifier`). Never log session IDs, invite codes, usernames, file paths, message content, or media names.
- **Documentation:** update §13.2 of the #267 report with how to enable the logs, what the output looks like, and how to aggregate it into `results.csv`.

## Out of scope

- Structured logging, log shipping, CloudWatch metrics, and alarms (#166).
- OpenTelemetry tracing and a Jaeger/Aspire setup (a separate follow-up, planned with #166 and #164).
- Enabling timing logs by default on hosted environments.
- Automated collection of native client marks. React Native DevTools shows them interactively; automated native collection is an open question.
- Any optimization or claim of improvement.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The three decision-gate conditions are recorded in an issue comment before implementation starts.
- [ ] With the variable unset, server output is byte-for-byte unchanged. With it set, each non-excluded request emits exactly one `http_timing` JSON line with method, route template, status, duration, and timestamp.
- [ ] Every route handled in `server/src/http.ts` maps to a template, and unmatched paths map to `other`. Tests prove that no ID, invite code, or path parameter appears in the output, following the audit redaction tests.
- [ ] Streaming media responses are tagged and realtime event streams are excluded, with tests.
- [ ] Overhead is measured with autocannon with logging on vs off. The p50 difference is within run-to-run variance (reported in the PR) or below an explicitly stated threshold.
- [ ] Job execution time and queue wait can be exported for at least the clip-processing and film-compile jobs.
- [ ] J1–J3 marks appear in the Chrome Performance panel (web) and the React Native DevTools Performance panel (iOS), with screenshots, and are readable by a sitespeed.io run on web.
- [ ] With the build flag unset, no marks and no extra output are produced.
- [ ] The #267 report (§13.2) is updated and links this issue's PR.
- [ ] Delivered in one focused, reviewed PR targeting `dev`.

## Dependencies

- Depends on the #267 recommendation being accepted.
- Coordinate with #166 (structured logs, metrics, alarms): shared field names and redaction rules, one logging approach.
- Lays groundwork for the OpenTelemetry follow-up (related to #164, the SQS worker).
- Can provide data for #175 (SQLite measurement) and #309 (press feedback).
- Cold-launch timing must account for the 600 ms branded launch floor once #243 lands.

## Delivery note

This is a conditional proposal. The acceptance criteria allow a no-implementation outcome: if external tools prove sufficient, record that decision in the #267 report and close this issue.

## User outcome

Taps feel acknowledged and navigation feels continuous rather than abrupt or frozen.

## Scope

Entry/navigation interaction tests, iPhone touch review, keyboard and reduced-motion checks. **Stop if:** animation delays input, masks errors, or breaks accessibility.

<!-- sprint2:issue-key=self-registration-api -->

## User outcome

A visitor can create a real Rewind username/password account without an administrator creating it first.

## Scope

Add a public registration API using the existing real-account model and password storage. Validate and normalize username/password input, limit automated abuse and duplicate attempts, and create an account with no inherited Demo or private-group membership. Keep administrator provisioning and reset for pilot support. Registration success leads to normal sign-in; it does not bypass the existing session or group rules.

## Acceptance


1. A new visitor registers over HTTPS, then signs in with the created credentials; duplicate or malformed usernames and weak passwords are rejected without partial accounts.
2. Passwords use the existing slow salted storage and never appear in logs, URLs or responses. Registration is rate limited, and repeated requests cannot silently create multiple accounts.
3. The account has no access to a group until its owner creates one or accepts a valid invitation. Demo identities cannot register as or be upgraded into real accounts.
4. Existing administrator-created accounts and current sign-in/session tests continue to work; migrations preserve existing data.

## Verification and stop condition

Server tests for success, duplicate/invalid/rate-limited attempts, Demo separation, private-group denial, migration upgrade, and a live HTTPS test account after the normal auth/infrastructure review. **Stop if:** public registration would expose private data or require plaintext credential handling.

## Reported evidence
The supplied phone screenshots show that Create account only says an administrator must create pilot accounts. The user explicitly requested self-registration; this supersedes the earlier pilot policy in #169.

<!-- sprint2:issue-key=hosted-auth-transport -->

## User outcome

A hosted page advertising Sign in can reach its real-account service and give a truthful session state.

## Scope

Diagnose the observed `403 auth_transport_unavailable` on `/api/auth/session`. Coordinate the app, reverse proxy, CloudFront forwarding and trusted HTTPS/origin policy with #230 and #243. Keep direct insecure-origin access denied. Fix the entry message so a server configuration or outage is not misreported as the person's connection problem.

## Acceptance


1. On each advertised real-login HTTPS hostname, an unsigned session check returns the expected unauthenticated state, not `auth_transport_unavailable`; a known pilot account can sign in, reload, and sign out from mobile web.
2. Secure first-party cookies reach the API and remain `Secure`, `HttpOnly` and `SameSite`; native Authorization requests work on their intended HTTPS origin. No credential or session token appears in a URL or log.
3. The origin rejects forged HTTPS assertions and direct public HTTP sign-in. If the legacy Demo host cannot support real login, its entry screen clearly routes to the supported account host or does not advertise Sign in/Create account until that host is ready.
4. Offline, expired session, and server-unavailable messages state what happened and offer an appropriate retry without blaming the user's connection when the service is at fault.

## Verification and stop condition

Read-only hosted health/session probes; valid and invalid pilot-account journeys on the reviewed live environment; relevant auth, proxy and web tests. **Stop if:** the fix requires weakening origin trust, sending credentials over HTTP, or applying Terraform before a human reviews the exact plan.

## Reported evidence
Read-only probe of https://d3ito43l174cl7.cloudfront.net/ on 30 September 2026: `/api/health` returned 200; unauthenticated `/api/auth/session` returned 403 `auth_transport_unavailable`. The phone screenshots also show a persistent sign-in-service warning.

title: Keep demo and runtime diagnostics off Home

body:
## Summary

`tests/responsive/accessibility.spec.ts:42` (`Home, Settings, Camera, Chat, and Archive have no serious or critical Axe violations`) intermittently fails the `toBeFocused()` assertion on `route-heading-archive`. Reproduced independently of any unrelated change, so this is a pre-existing race, not caused by a specific PR.

## Root cause

The route-focus effect in `App.tsx` focuses the heading once per route change and stops watching:

```ts
const focusHeading = () => { ... return true; };
if (focusHeading()) return; // stops here on first success
```

Archive renders a `loading` heading first, then replaces it with the loaded-state heading once data resolves. If that swap happens after the first focus but the effect already returned, the old heading node is removed from the DOM and focus falls back to `<body>`. Under parallel Playwright workers (slower page load), this window is hit often enough to fail.

## Evidence

- 6/6 pass running the spec alone, sequentially.
- `npx playwright test tests/responsive/accessibility.spec.ts:42 --repeat-each 40 --workers 8`: 9/40 failed, consistently on `route-heading-archive`, all `Expected: focused / Received: inactive`.
- Same failure observed on an unrelated CI run (PR #257) and is independent of that PR's changes.

## Acceptance criteria

- The route-focus effect keeps watching for heading replacement (not just first success) for its existing 5s window, and only refocuses when the previously-focused heading has left the DOM and focus has fallen back to `<body>` (so it never steals focus from a user who has already tabbed elsewhere).
- `npx playwright test tests/responsive/accessibility.spec.ts --repeat-each 40 --workers 8` passes 40/40 for the affected test.
- Existing responsive/accessibility suite (19 tests) and Jest suite continue to pass.

## Out of scope

Any other flaky test; other route heading behavior.
title: Flaky Archive route-focus check under parallel Playwright load

## How to review (about 10 minutes)

1. Under each phone, 👍 every direction you like, ❤️ one top pick, and write pros and cons. Do the same for the docks below the phones (👍 one or two of A, D, E, G).
2. When you're done, press **Copy, then comment in the issue** at the bottom, paste here and click **Comment**.
3. To change your review, edit on the page and send again. Only your latest comment counts.

Please don't edit the hidden first line of your comment; it holds your votes.

## Proposal

- **Navigation:** Home / Chat / Archive plus a separate shutter; Settings moves into the avatar (draft). This replaces the five tabs, so it needs a team decision.
- **Data shown before the reveal:** only the count, who is in, and the countdown. Never how many moments each other person added.
- Waiting members aren't named by default, and each member has their own colour (ideas from Reveal, Capsule and Capsl).

## Questions

1. Which two or three directions feel most like a private time capsule with close friends?
2. Should we move to three tabs plus a shutter? Which dock: A, D, E or G?
3. Should the reveal be a shared "watch at the same time" premiere?

## Objective

Prepare a human-reviewed research brief recommending how the team can later profile and improve Rewind's performance, and show a credible before/after difference. Focus on local, CLI-driven tools with a visual dashboard, timeline, or trace view similar to the investigation experience of AWS X-Ray. Rewind uses Expo/React Native for iOS and web, with an optional local Node runtime, so assess which layers each candidate can actually measure.

This issue is for research and discussion only. Running the app through a full performance campaign, implementing instrumentation, optimizing code, and claiming measured improvements are follow-up work after this week.

## Research scope

- Compare suitable local profiling and performance-testing options. Cover CLI and automation support; dashboard, trace, timeline, or flame-graph views; fit for Expo/React Native (iOS simulator/device and web) and the optional Node runtime; setup effort; local data handling; licensing/cost; and export or screenshot capabilities.
- Recommend representative user journeys and a repeatable future baseline-versus-follow-up method. Identify useful metrics and controls (same device/build/data/state, warm-up and repeat counts, and relevant runtime conditions) so future comparisons are credible.
- Explain how to capture and collate evidence: app screenshots for matching states, profiler/dashboard views, traces or raw measurements, and the run metadata needed to interpret them. Use only synthetic/local test data.
- Give a reasoned recommendation, alternatives and trade-offs, setup outline, limitations, open questions, and the next issue(s) needed to conduct actual profiling.

## Suggested work split

- **Jiayu Jiang:** survey local CLI profiler and dashboard/trace options, and assess their fit for the Expo/React Native client and local Node service.
- **Nguyễn Kim Long:** propose representative performance scenarios and metrics, and research the repeatable baseline/after and screenshot/evidence-capture workflow.
- **Both:** record findings and source links in this issue, review each other's conclusions, reconcile overlaps, and agree on the recommendation. The final brief must show the researchers' own evaluation and judgment; an agent-generated summary alone is not the deliverable.

Please confirm or adjust this split in an issue comment so the ownership is explicit.

## Proposed schedule (Singapore time)

- **Mon, Sep 28:** confirm the split, target journeys, and comparison criteria.
- **Tue, Sep 29:** independent tool/method research; add findings and links to this issue.
- **Wed, Sep 30 morning:** compare conclusions, resolve open questions, and finish the brief; discuss/submit by **12:00 SGT**.
- Schedule actual profiling separately after Sep 30, once the recommendation is reviewed.

## Deliverable

A reviewable document at `doc/planning/performance-profiling-research.md`, linked from this issue, with a concise comparison matrix, source links, chosen recommendation and rationale, future run/evidence-capture procedure, contributor split, and unresolved decisions.

## Acceptance criteria

- The research brief is linked here by Wed, Sep 30, 2026, 12:00 SGT, and reflects review and judgment by both named researchers.
- It compares relevant local tools against the criteria above and recommends a practical toolchain for this app's client and local service boundaries.
- It describes a reproducible future baseline/after protocol and how to capture matching app screenshots plus profiler/dashboard and measurement evidence.
- It identifies limitations, open decisions, and concrete follow-up work for actual profiling.
- No app instrumentation, optimization, or full performance campaign is required or expected in this issue.
