title: TASK: Research local performance profiling and before/after evidence

body:
## Problem

The proposal (§6, General Architecture) names **PostgreSQL** as the relational store for users, groups, memberships, invitations, cycles, contribution metadata, prompts, notification preferences, chat and processing state. Hosted dev still keeps all of this in one SQLite file on the Lightsail host. The earlier conditional framing ("only if SQLite hits measured limits") is superseded: the owner decided on 7 Oct 2026 that the proposal's PostgreSQL requirement is in scope.

## Expected

- The server runs unchanged on PostgreSQL when `REWIND_DATABASE_URL` is set. Local runs and the default tests keep SQLite.
- Hosted dev uses managed PostgreSQL (Lightsail, PostgreSQL 17):
  - private, encrypted at rest, TLS verified;
  - separate least-privilege app and read-only logins created by Terraform, never handled by hand.
- Hosted data moves from the latest S3 backup into PostgreSQL in one transaction, with per-table row-count and content-hash reconciliation; nothing is committed unless it is exact.
- Cutover and rollback are one reviewed switch (`cutover` in `infra/terraform/media/database.tf`). The SQLite file stays untouched for rollback.
- Each database is bound to one environment, and a runtime pointed at another environment's database refuses to start.
- Authorized operators can inspect live rows: the read-only `/admin` browser, or psql/pgAdmin through an SSH tunnel as the read-only role.

## How to check

- `npm run test:fast` passes, and the Quality job **Server tests on PostgreSQL** passes. The whole server suite runs against PostgreSQL 17, plus `server/tests/postgres.test.mjs` (import, reconciliation, rollback-on-mismatch, schema parity, reconnect, environment binding, roles).
- Run the **Database operations** workflow:
  - `bootstrap`, then `import`: the summary lists every table's reconciled row count;
  - set `cutover = true`, then Deploy dev;
  - `status` reports engine `postgresql`, ready, migration 30/30, environment `dev`.
- On the hosted URL: sign in with an existing account, open its group and chat history, and send a message.

Design: `docs/architecture/ADR-0003-postgresql.md`. Runbook: `docs/architecture/postgresql-operations.md`.

body:
## User outcome
Clip capture and Settings behave predictably at the edges: portrait phone videos are accepted, the preview is there when you need it, settings you change stick, and Home doesn't block paths that are still allowed.

## Scope
Six smaller problems found while reviewing #256. None of them block that PR.

1. **Portrait check ignores rotation.** Picked videos are checked with raw width/height, but phones often store portrait video as landscape frames plus a rotation flag. #256 already handles this on the server; the client doesn't, so some Android phones may reject a real portrait video. (`src/capture/platform.ts:555`)
2. **Preview disappears after a cancelled or failed upload.** `previewLocked` only resets when a new clip is picked, so you can't re-watch the unsent clip before retrying. (`src/capture/VideoCaptureScreen.tsx:293`)
3. **Language and Debug settings can snap back on first launch.** If they change before AsyncStorage finishes loading, the stored value overwrites the change. (`src/i18n/LanguageProvider.tsx:49`, `src/debug/DebugProvider.tsx:113`)
4. **Home "Add a moment" is disabled once the allowance is used.** Stills don't use the allowance, and replacing a clip also starts from Camera, so the button blocks more than it should. (`src/capsule/CapsuleSummary.tsx:304`)
5. **The review screen claims checks that never happened.** Picked videos are hard-coded as `hasAudio: true` (Expo Image Picker doesn't report audio), and the review says "audio track detected". A silent video is trimmed and uploaded in full, then rejected by the server without saying why. Native recording has the same problem: `recordAsync()` only guarantees `uri`, so width, height, duration and audio fall back to `720×1280`, measured time and `true`, and the "audio included" copy isn't verified either. (`src/capture/platform.ts:564`, `src/capture/platform.ts:592`)
6. **Cancelling a recording leaves the video file behind.** Cancel calls `stopRecording()`, so `recordAsync()` still returns a clip and it gets copied into `rewind-clips`. `BoundedVideoRecordingSession.start()` then sees the recording was cancelled and throws, but never deletes the copied file. Start–cancel a few times and the cache fills with clips that should be gone, until the next cold-start sweep. This was already on `dev`; #256 didn't touch it. (`src/capture/video-recording.ts:67`)

## Outside this issue
The merge blockers from the same review (#258) and any redesign of the capture flow.

## Acceptance
- A portrait phone video stored with a 90° or 270° rotation is accepted on both iOS and Android.
- After a cancelled or failed upload, the member can open the preview again before retrying. The preview stays hidden once a clip is submitted.
- A language or Debug change made during first-launch loading is kept after loading finishes and after a restart.
- With the allowance used, Home still leads to Camera for stills and clip replacement, and clearly says that no new clips can be submitted.
- Audio, size and duration that the client can't actually read are treated as unknown, not filled in. Before upload, the review copy says the server will check them instead of saying they were detected.
- A silent video is rejected with a message that says it needs audio.
- A cancelled recording leaves no file in `rewind-clips`, and there's a test that checks the file is actually deleted, not just that the review screen stays closed.
- Each change has a test.

## Relevant code
`src/capture/platform.ts`; `src/capture/video-recording.ts`; `src/capture/VideoCaptureScreen.tsx`; `src/i18n/LanguageProvider.tsx`; `src/debug/DebugProvider.tsx`; `src/capsule/CapsuleSummary.tsx`

## Dependencies
#256

## Verification
`npm run test:fast`; for Home changes also `npm run test:responsive`; check the rotation case on a real Android phone.

## Delivery
One focused PR from `dev` into `dev` after #256 merges.

title: Follow-up capture and settings edge cases from #256 review

body:
## User outcome
A member can take a still without being asked for the microphone, upload a phone video that is about 15 seconds long, gets an honest message when their allowance is used up, and never sees fake Debug data outside a development build.

## Scope
Four problems found while reviewing #256:

1. **Library videos around 15 s fail on upload.** `pickLibraryVideo` accepts up to 15.1 s and reports the duration as 15, but the server checks the real file length and rejects anything over 15 s. A "15-second" iPhone Camera clip (usually ~15.03 s) passes review, then fails with a vague error. (`src/capture/platform.ts:550`)
2. **Hitting the contribution limit says "retake".** The `quota_exceeded` reason only reaches the status panel in the synthetic Demo path. On a real upload it is dropped, so the member is told to retake and hits the same limit again. (`src/capture/VideoCaptureScreen.tsx:821`)
3. **Debug mode is available to everyone and stays on.** The Settings toggle is not limited to development builds, and its state (including "offline" and forced scenarios) survives restarts. (`src/settings/SettingsScreen.tsx:319`, `src/debug/DebugProvider.tsx`)
4. **The still camera asks for the microphone.** #256 turns on `autoRequestPermission` for `CameraCaptureScreen` (`App.tsx:461`), which calls the shared `requestPermissions()` and asks for camera and microphone. Tapping "Add a moment" to take a still now shows two system prompts in a row. Worse, `cameraAccessStatus()` requires both permissions, so a member who allows the camera but declines the microphone can't take a still either. (`src/capture/capture-state.ts:43`)

## Outside this issue
The follow-up polish items from the same review (#259), real-account sessions (#242–#244), and any change to the server's 15-second limit.

## Acceptance
- A library video slightly over 15 s is either rejected on the phone with a clear message, or trimmed to 15 s so the server accepts it. It never passes review and then fails on upload.
- A real upload rejected for `quota_exceeded` shows "Contribution limit reached" and does not suggest retaking.
- Debug mode cannot be turned on in a production build, and a debug state saved earlier has no effect there.
- The still camera only checks and asks for the camera. Allowing the camera is enough to take a still, whatever the microphone permission is.
- The clip screen asks for the camera, then the microphone, only when the member opens it.
- Still and clip access are worked out separately, instead of sharing one "needs both permissions" status.
- Each fix has a test.

## Relevant code
`App.tsx`; `src/capture/platform.ts`; `src/capture/capture-state.ts`; `src/capture/CameraCaptureScreen.tsx`; `src/capture/VideoCaptureScreen.tsx`; `src/capture/contribution-status.tsx`; `src/settings/SettingsScreen.tsx`; `src/debug/DebugProvider.tsx`

## Dependencies
#256

## Verification
`npm run test:fast`; on a real iPhone, open Camera for the first time and confirm only the camera prompt appears; pick a ~15 s video and upload it against the local runtime.

## Delivery
Fix on `ui-concept/home-atelier` before #256 merges.

The Quality workflow currently starts for every pull request and for pushes to `main`, including changes that cannot affect application behavior. For example, PR #237 changed only files under `skills/` but still ran the full check suite.

Configure CI triggers so documentation-only changes do not start CI on any existing trigger, including pushes and pull requests. Changes that include runnable code or GitHub Actions workflow configuration must still start the existing checks. When a change includes both documentation and runnable code, CI must start.

## Acceptance criteria

- Changes limited to documentation, including documentation-only changes under `docs/` and `skills/`, do not start CI on pushes or pull requests.
- Changes to application code or GitHub Actions workflow configuration start the existing checks.
- Changes combining documentation with application code or workflow configuration start the existing checks.
- Existing CI triggers continue to cover the relevant branches and pull request events.

## Out of scope

Changes to check requirements or how GitHub treats skipped checks.

## Related

[#229 — Establish protected dev integration branch and on-demand main promotions](https://github.com/Collaboration95/rewind-app/issues/229)

## Overview

This is my updated Home concept for #189.

It builds on the existing Today version, including its Camera flow and debug mode. I redesigned the Home screen to make the prompt, reveal status, remaining allowance, and main action easier to understand.

This direction is called **Atelier**.

## What changed

The new Home screen includes:

- A large sealed-photo card for the current prompt
- Clear sealed, developing, delayed, and released states
- The remaining reveal time
- A film strip showing the remaining contribution allowance
- One clear main action: `Add a moment`, `Check Archive`, or `Watch group film`
- A simpler group and member summary
- A warmer darkroom-inspired visual style

The photo card is only an illustration. It does not show any unrevealed group media.

## What stays the same

This update keeps the existing Today flow, including:

- The five main navigation tabs
- The Camera flow and debug mode
- The labelled local Demo
- Photo and clip contribution states
- Contribution count and duration limits
- Sealed media protection before reveal
- Film playback through Archive after release
- Existing loading, empty, denied, error, and retry states

No runtime or data contract change is intended.

## Branch

[`ui-concept/home-atelier`](https://github.com/Collaboration95/rewind-app/tree/ui-concept/home-atelier)

## Checks so far

Passed:

- ESLint
- Architecture check
- TypeScript
- Expo Web build

I also checked the top and bottom of the Home screen at:

- 320 x 568
- 375 x 667
- 360 x 740
- 390 x 844
- 1280 x 800

The bottom navigation stayed visible, and the final Home content did not overlap it.

Still to do before opening a draft PR:

- Format three changed files
- Update five Home tests that still expect the old layout
- Complete the automated responsive run
- Test on Android and an iPhone 14 or newer simulator
- Check the web version in a second browser engine

## Feedback

Please try these tasks:

1. Find the current prompt, reveal time, and remaining allowance.
2. Add or simulate a contribution and check whether its sealed state is clear.
3. Find the released film, or understand why it is not available yet.
4. Check whether the Home screen feels clear on both phone and desktop.

Please mention anything that was confusing and which parts of Atelier, Today, Darkroom, or Polaroid you prefer.

## About #208

#208 contains my earlier Darkroom and Polaroid explorations. It remains available as design history, while this issue is the current Atelier direction for review.

This is still a UI concept. It is not a decision to merge the design into `main` or deploy it.

<!-- sprint2:issue-key=entry-login-client -->
## User outcome
A person enters an existing real username/password once, stays signed in, and can sign out on web and iPhone Expo Go. Accounts may be self-registered under #307/#308 or provisioned by an administrator.

## Login and loading screen wireframe
Implement the two entry screens shown in the supplied wireframes:

- **Loading screen:** show the Rewind wordmark and tagline centered in the screen while the app loads. Keep this screen free of actions and other content.
- **Login screen:** show the Rewind wordmark and tagline in the upper portion of the screen. Place two prominent actions near the bottom, in this order: **Create account**, then **Sign in**. Keep the layout legible and usable on web, iPhone, and Android.
- **Create account:** keep this as a distinct route. The current administrator-guidance page is interim; #308 replaces it with a working signup flow backed by #307. This issue remains focused on sign-in and session restore.
- **Sign in:** open the username/password form for an existing provisioned account.

## Scope
Build the login form and session provider; use the first-party cookie on web and SecureStore on native; attach the real session to API requests; show wrong-password, offline, expiry and admin-reset guidance. Implement the loading and login entry layouts described above.

## Outside this issue
Native OIDC redirects, the registration API and signup form tracked by #307/#308, or Demo identity as a real account.

## Acceptance
- Web, iPhone Expo Go and Android can sign in against the HTTPS API and restore a session after restart.
- The loading screen presents the Rewind wordmark and tagline centered without actions; the login screen presents the wordmark/tagline and the **Create account** and **Sign in** actions in the wireframe order.
- **Create account** remains a distinct entry action; its working signup outcome is accepted under #308. **Sign in** opens the existing-account form and works for both self-registered and administrator-created accounts.
- Sign out and server expiry clear protected views; wrong password/offline have useful messages.
- No real token is placed in AsyncStorage, a URL, a log, or a Demo profile selector.

## Relevant code
App.tsx; src/session; src/runtime/local-runtime-client.ts; tests/App.test.tsx

## Dependencies
entry-brand-welcome, entry-session-api

## Verification
npm run test:fast; web login; physical iPhone Expo Go login against dev HTTPS

## Stop condition
Stop if a native token must be stored in unprotected AsyncStorage or password traffic is plain HTTP.

## Delivery
One focused PR from `dev` into `dev`. Request human review for authentication, database, private access, and deployment changes. Keep the parent epic open until its integrated flow works.


## Updated product direction (30 September 2026)
The user requested self-registration and a functioning hosted entry. #307 and #308 supersede the administrator-only placeholder; #305 tracks the hosted HTTPS auth transport needed for live sign-in. The [Sprint 2 user journey plan](https://github.com/Collaboration95/rewind-app/blob/dev/doc/planning/sprints/sprint-2-user-journey-plan.md) records the prior pilot baseline.


## Updated product direction (30 September 2026): cold launch and welcome screen

The owner supplied two screenshots. The hand-drawn loading/login wireframe is the desired direction; the current-app screenshot documents the welcome page that should be simplified. The service error visible in that screenshot is incidental and is not part of this UI request. The owner will attach the wireframe image directly to this issue.

### Cold-launch screen

- On a cold launch, show a deliberate Rewind loading screen with the wordmark and tagline centered, with no controls or extra copy.
- Keep it visible for at least 600 ms on cold launches and until app initialization is ready, so launch never flashes as a black/blank glitch.
- Do not add a forced delay to warm launches.

### Welcome screen

- Follow the supplied wireframe: Rewind branding and tagline, then **Create account** and **Sign in** near the bottom.
- Remove **Try Demo** and its explanatory copy from the welcome/entry screen. Do not replace it with another Demo entry action.
- Remove repeated brand marks, repeated taglines, and extra welcome prose so the screen stays simple.
- Keep Create account and Sign in connected to their existing account flows; registration behavior remains tracked by #307 and #308.

### Acceptance additions

- A cold launch visibly presents the branded loading screen for at least 600 ms and leaves it only when initialization is ready; a warm launch is not artificially delayed.
- The welcome screen contains only the brand/tagline and the Create account and Sign in actions; no Try Demo action or Demo explanatory copy appears there.
- The screen hierarchy follows the attached wireframe and remains usable on web, iPhone and Android.

## Outcome
Before creating the two live environments, design the AWS architecture and its full operating lifecycle so dev can be tested continuously and release stays stable, private, recoverable, and within a known cost ceiling.

## Scope
- Inventory the current Lightsail host, CloudFront/web path, DNS/TLS, SQLite/media paths, worker, Terraform state, deployment scripts, backup/restore scripts, budgets, and current shutdown behavior. Link exact repository files and verified AWS facts where needed.
- Draw the proposed request/data path for **dev** and **release**: two independently addressable web/API origins, separate Lightsail application data and media, distinct Terraform state and names, secrets/IAM, backups, build version, and health checks. Explain where a member's password/session lives and how the PWA and Expo Go reach the HTTPS API.
- Specify lifecycle states and transitions: provision -> deploy -> serve -> quiesce writes -> consistent backup -> optional stop/OFF -> restore/restart -> health check -> rollback. Identify which environment stays live by default; a dev power schedule must never stop release or discard private data.
- Define deploy/promotion ownership, review points, an immutable commit/version stamp, database migration/rollback behavior, test-data boundaries, minimum logs/alerts, and a recovery smoke.
- Give an itemized monthly baseline and stopped-state estimate for both environments, plus a cost ceiling and the changes needed in #230 and #190. Include risk from the existing one-state/fixed-name Terraform root.

## Acceptance
1. A concise architecture diagram and decision summary are posted in this issue, with links to the relevant repo configuration. Dev/release boundaries, request flow, storage, sessions, and worker are unambiguous.
2. A lifecycle table names triggers, preconditions, irreversible steps, recovery action, and owner for each transition. It states how the current OFF-state defect in #190 is addressed or deliberately deferred.
3. A concrete implementation sequence splits #230 into reviewable changes and names a smoke test that proves dev cannot read or mutate release data.
4. The cost model and rollback/recovery limits are reviewed before any Terraform apply or AWS resource creation. Record any remaining values in #169.

## Outside this issue
No Terraform apply, deployment, resource deletion, production data copy, new IAM grants, or daily promotion schedule. Implementation follows in #230 and focused PRs.

## Verification / handoff
Review the diagram and lifecycle against current repo scripts, Terraform plan output when safely available, and the existing host evidence. Stop and request the owner decision if domains, account permissions, cost ceiling, or desired OFF policy cannot be established without live AWS changes.

# Workshop: run Rewind on your iPhone

Each collaborator should try the current `dev` build on their own iPhone. The normal workflow is just: pull `dev`, then run `make run` from the Rewind app directory.

## Before you start

- The Rewind repository is checked out locally and dependencies are installed. If this is a fresh checkout, run `npm ci` once.
- Your checkout is on the `dev` branch.
- Your iPhone and Mac are on the same reachable Wi-Fi network.
- Have an iPhone runtime compatible with this project's Expo SDK. If public Expo Go reports an SDK version mismatch, ask the workshop lead for the compatible runtime; tunnel mode does not fix a version mismatch.

## Run it

From the Rewind app directory:

```sh
git pull origin dev
make run
```

When Expo prints a QR code, scan it with the iPhone Camera app and open Rewind in the compatible runtime. The launcher starts the local SQLite/FFmpeg service and Expo over LAN. For the web UI, press `w` in the terminal; web and iPhone use the same local backend.

Use the synthetic Demo identities and non-sensitive test media. When finished, press Ctrl-C to stop Expo and the local service.

## Report your result

Comment with your `dev` commit SHA and whether Rewind opened and worked on your iPhone. Include your iPhone model, iOS version, runtime/version, and any blocker. Attach a screenshot of Rewind on your own phone if available; redact private details.

This checks the local development flow. It does not prove hosted processing, release, or recovery.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Each collaborator pulls the latest `dev` branch and runs `make run`.
- [ ] Each collaborator opens and tries Rewind on their own physical iPhone using a compatible runtime.
- [ ] Each collaborator records the commit SHA and PASS/BLOCKED result in an issue comment.

These are my two UI directions for #189, based on `main` at `525d3e5`. They are alternatives for one contributor, not the team's final choice. My Darkroom branch is separate from Loi's Darkroom draft PR #201. Both keep the five tabs and existing Demo/capture/reveal behavior. Neither has been merged.

## The two directions

| | Darkroom | Polaroid |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Home | Dark film-lab look, a swipeable and moving **illustrative** film roll, clear countdown, prompt and remaining allowance | Warm paper look, a stacked **illustrative** instant-photo frame, softer wording, countdown, prompt and quota progress |
| Across the app | Darkroom colours and compact cards | Warm colours across all pages and the bottom navigation |

Shared changes from `main`: member switching and runtime status move from Home to Settings; the fake sealed-media tiles are removed. Camera puts the live preview and shutter before the explanation cards, with scrolling. Archive can scroll without hiding its last content behind the bottom navigation. The copy separates a still saved on this device, a clip submitted/processing/sealed, and a film released in Archive. Illustrations never show unrevealed group media.

## References and choices

- [Lapse](https://lapse.com/): disposable-camera feeling and a friends-only journal. We kept the private, film-like mood, not its social/account model.
- [Reveal](https://joinreveal.app/): participation can be known while clips stay hidden; group clips become one later video. We kept the sealed-versus-released distinction, not its fixed daily recording schedule or stacked-video format.
- [1 Second Everyday](https://help.1se.co/en/articles/1077034-freestyle-vs-freestyle-collab-vs-journal): friends can add short snippets to one project; [its mash flow](https://help.1se.co/en/articles/3706409-how-to-create-a-mashed-video) makes a film from snippets. We kept the contribution-versus-film distinction, not early preview or manual editing.
- Our [earlier Rewind Figma design](https://www.figma.com/design/r1fRPAMj6BNcOTlXpNs666?node-id=11-2) guided the Darkroom rolling-film Home component.

## States and review

Both versions retain the existing loading, empty/offline, permission-denied/retry, local-still, clip queued/processing/sealed, and reveal locked/delayed/released paths. Before release, there is no clip thumbnail or playback. These are UI changes; no runtime or data contract was changed.

Local branches: `ui-concept/jiayu-darkroom` and `ui-concept/jiayu-polaroid`. Shareable branches, draft PRs and design links still need to be added. Loi Phan: please try both using the same three tasks—find the prompt/time/quota; make or simulate a contribution and understand its sealed state; find the film or understand why it is unavailable. Please note any problem and which direction you prefer.

## Checks so far

- Each branch: 347 Jest tests passed. Format, lint, architecture and TypeScript checks passed.
- Each responsive run printed 24 passing checks, but the runner did not exit cleanly and was stopped. Full `npm run check` stopped at three Docker-dependent deployment tests because Docker is unavailable on this machine.
- Both Expo iOS bundles and local LAN runtime health endpoints returned HTTP 200. Jiayu reports a quick iPhone walkthrough with no obvious issue; two recordings are attached below. This is not the required full native test record.
- Android, iPhone 14+ simulator, manual Chromium/Firefox-or-Safari walkthroughs, and peers' firsthand reviews are still pending. Keep the two concepts separate; do not merge or deploy as part of this issue.

## Problem

The hosted Lightsail HTTPS distribution needs to reach the web proxy on the instance. Compose currently publishes the web service only on loopback, so the distribution cannot use it as an HTTP origin.

## Scope

- Make the web service bind address configurable while keeping the local Compose default on 127.0.0.1:8080.
- Configure the hosted environment to publish the web proxy on the interface and port required by the Lightsail distribution.
- Keep the Node runtime host binding loopback-only.
- Make the disposable lifecycle smoke test force loopback settings, regardless of hosted values inherited from the shell.
- Document the host environment update, service recreation, firewall requirements, and distribution-level verification.
- Cover local and hosted Compose port mappings and lifecycle-test environment isolation.

## Acceptance criteria

- Local Compose still exposes the web proxy only on loopback by default.
- The hosted configuration allows the Lightsail distribution to reach the web origin on the required port, while the runtime remains loopback-only.
- Firewall guidance accounts for origin reachability and avoids unnecessary direct public access where the platform permits restricting it.
- The lifecycle smoke test cannot inherit a public hosted bind address.
- Automated checks cover the resolved local/hosted mappings and environment isolation.
- The deployment runbook describes verifying the public HTTPS URL and /api/health through the distribution; loopback checks alone are insufficient.
- The hosting change is manually verified against the deployed distribution before being considered complete.

## Context

Exploratory changes are in deploy/README.md, deploy/compose.yaml, deploy/lifecycle-smoke.mjs, deploy/rewind.env.example, tests/deploy/host-lifecycle-smoke.test.mjs, and tests/web-deployment.test.mjs. # Sprint 2 iOS acceptance check

Date: 2026-09-25  
Repository: `Collaboration95/rewind-app`  
Commit checked: `525d3e539151b2f854a59d73c82b33e02f67d1cd` (`main`)  
Device: iPhone 15 Pro Simulator, iOS 17.5, Expo Go 57.0.9  
Runtime: isolated local SQLite/FFmpeg service at `127.0.0.1:8787`; synthetic camera mode enabled. No AWS resources or real media were used.

## Findings

### P1 — iOS Chat realtime never connects (#153)

On the Chat tab, the simulator displayed `Chat connection: Reconnecting…` and this error: `This platform does not provide EventSource. Supply an eventSourceFactory for LAN realtime support.` Tapping `Retry chat connection` left the same state. This prevents native iOS from receiving the realtime events needed for off-tab unread counts and reconnect behavior.

Evidence points to the default runtime constructing `RealtimeChatClient` without a native EventSource implementation; `src/chat/realtime-client.ts:122-133` throws when `globalThis.EventSource` is absent. This is a reproducible native acceptance failure, despite passing browser and automated checks.

### P1 — Local reveal control throws before it can report cycle state

With the local runtime connected and Amber as group owner, Settings → **Start local reveal** displayed `Cannot read property 'request' of undefined`. The call first advances the cycle, then fails when it calls the detached `revealDemoCycle` method. In `App.tsx:740`, the method is copied from the client and then invoked at `App.tsx:759`; `LocalRuntimeClient` methods call `this.request(...)`. Preserve the receiver or call the method directly, and add a regression test using a class-backed runtime client.

The documented local mobile capture-to-reveal flow cannot complete through this button until this is fixed. The isolated-runtime full-cycle backend scenario passes separately, so this failure is in the app integration path.

### P2 — Seeded contribution disagrees with visible allowance totals (#158)

On Home, the ledger showed `Submission 1`, `demo-contribution`, sealed, 3 seconds, with the row stating it uses one contribution and 3 seconds. Before a new capture, the totals showed 0/5 and 0/30 seconds. After creating a synthetic 2-second contribution, the totals showed 1/5 and 2/30 seconds while the ledger showed both the 3-second and 2-second entries. The isolated database confirms both records are attached to the current cycle.

This makes the contribution history and allowance summary disagree in the local Demo. Align the seeded fixture accounting with its contribution row, or change the displayed row/impact if it is intentionally excluded.

### P2 — Fresh Demo fixture reports missing ready outputs (#171)

On the newly initialized isolated runtime, read-only `consistency --json` reported two non-repairable `missing_output` findings: `demo-clip` and `demo-film`. Both seeded jobs have status `ready` but no `output_path`; neither file exists. A new unmodified local runtime therefore starts with consistency findings. Decide whether these placeholders should be excluded from the audit or seeded with valid outputs.

## Checks that passed

- `npm run check` on this exact `main`: formatting, lint, architecture, typecheck, 31 root tests, 193 server tests, 347 Jest tests, and 6 accessibility browser tests.
- `npm run test:responsive`: 19/19 tests.
- `npm run test:full-cycle`: 1/1 (`reset → join → sealed clip → reveal → authorized archive`).
- `npm run server:preflight` on the isolated local runtime: service, SQLite fixture, LAN address, and FFmpeg gates passed.
- `retention --json` defaulted to dry-run and returned no candidates; no files were deleted.
- The simulator connected to the local runtime. Home displayed the cycle prompt and locked state; synthetic clip creation completed and reported `Contribution sealed`; Archive showed prompt/date/state metadata and stated that locked media had no playback or media links.

## Acceptance limits

- The simulator has no physical camera. The app correctly identified the synthetic fixture preview and said recording was unsupported there. Physical capture and device-camera evidence remain unverified.
- Hosted HTTPS acceptance, two clean hosted runs, rollback/recovery proof, and a genuine non-author run remain blocked by existing issue #145: the Lightsail instance/static IP/distribution were deleted, Terraform state is unreconciled, and there is no verified recovery point. No AWS operation was performed.
- The Archive UI was checked before release. The app-level reveal error prevented validating released-cycle playback in the simulator; the separate full-cycle backend scenario passed.

title: [Sprint 2 blocker] Native iOS Chat and local reveal fail on main

body:
## Type / priority

- **Type:** Infrastructure bug / lifecycle automation
- **Priority:** High — the Demo Lightsail instance and public distribution are currently deployed and may continue accruing charges.
- **Labels:** `bug`, `high priority`, `help wanted`

## Summary

Make the Rewind Demo lifecycle automation reach the same verified, resource-deleting OFF state as the local `infra/scripts/destroy-demo.sh` workflow. The current AWS Lambdas have not kept the deployed Demo off: the legacy power controller only issues Lightsail Stop/Start calls, while the cost-safety audit Lambda is report-only. A stopped Lightsail instance remains billable, and the separate public Lightsail distribution also needs to be deleted to end its recurring charge.

The workflow must back up and verify the application data before deleting anything, use Terraform as the infrastructure source of truth, report each state transition, and avoid automatic restarts while the desired state is OFF.

## User impact

- The live Demo endpoint remained available after the local shutdown workflow was expected to be used.
- A Lightsail instance and a deployed Lightsail distribution are present. These resources can accrue charges until deleted; a Stop call is not the bill-stopping action.
- The current notification/audit path does not itself execute the full shutdown workflow, so a successful notification or Lambda invocation must not be treated as proof that the Demo is OFF.

## Observed evidence (2026-09-24 investigation)

- Lightsail instance `rewind-demo` was **running**. It was created on 2026-09-21.
- Lightsail distribution `rewind-demo-web` was **Deployed and enabled**. Its endpoint uses a `cloudfront.net` hostname; it is a Lightsail distribution resource managed by `infra/terraform/demo/web-distribution.tf`.
- CloudTrail showed the old power-controller role calling `StopInstance` at 2026-09-17 14:53:04 UTC and `StartInstance` at 14:53:26 UTC. Those events predate the currently deployed instance and show the controller can reverse a stop almost immediately.
- The audit scheduler assumed its target role as recently as 2026-09-24 04:17 UTC, and inventory-read activity is visible through 2026-09-21. The available read-only role could not read the Lambda’s CloudWatch logs/metrics, so successful audit output and notification delivery could not be confirmed.
- Cost Explorer showed $0 through 2026-09-23. Since these resources were created recently and Cost Explorer data can lag, this does not establish that the resources are free.
- `./infra/scripts/destroy-demo.sh --dry-run` produced a guarded plan with **0 additions, 2 changes, 10 deletions**. A local working-tree change currently allows the exact planned deletion of `aws_lightsail_distribution.web[0]` in the plan guard; review and preserve or replace that fix.
- `./infra/scripts/destroy-demo.sh --apply --confirm` stopped at its required SSH backup step because the current executor is outside the configured SSH allowlist. The command did not upload the backup or reach Terraform apply. **No AWS resources were changed by that attempt.** Do not bypass this guard or widen SSH access without an explicitly reviewed, Terraform-managed change.

## Required state machine

```text
ACTIVE
  -> BACKUP_IN_PROGRESS
  -> BACKUP_VERIFIED
  -> OFF

OFF
  -> RESTORE_IN_PROGRESS
  -> HEALTH_CHECK
  -> ACTIVE

Any failure before BACKUP_VERIFIED:
  remain ACTIVE; notify with the failed step

Terraform failure after BACKUP_VERIFIED:
  remain recoverable; record the partial state and notify
  before retrying/reconciling
```

### State invariants

- **ACTIVE:** runtime exists; public distribution exists only if explicitly desired; the audit expects the configured approved active/stopped state. Any automatic start must be consistent with this desired state.
- **BACKUP_VERIFIED:** fresh database and media archives plus a valid manifest are uploaded to S3 and verified before destructive Terraform actions begin.
- **OFF:** no Demo Lightsail instance, retained/detached Demo static IP, public distribution, legacy power controller, or automatic-start schedule. The verified S3 recovery points and read-only cost-safety audit infrastructure remain. The audit expectation is `demo_off`.
- **RESTORE_IN_PROGRESS:** recreate only from an explicitly selected verified S3 recovery point; do not report ACTIVE until restore and health checks succeed. No automatic start is allowed while desired state is OFF.

## Work requested

1. **Complete the current safe teardown** using the existing guarded shutdown workflow once an approved SSH/backup execution route is available. Keep backup, manifest validation, S3 upload/readback, Terraform plan guard, and apply ordering intact. If access is still blocked, report the exact dependency and leave AWS resources unchanged.
2. **Define one desired-state source of truth** for ACTIVE/OFF and a documented, configurable rule for when the Demo is considered idle enough to tear down. Ensure start automation cannot immediately reverse an OFF transition.
3. **Implement a secure lifecycle executor** that invokes the same version-controlled backup/validation/Terraform workflow used locally. Evaluate an AWS-managed runner/orchestrator and a secure host backup mechanism (for example, SSM if it is deliberately installed/configured, or a dedicated trusted runner). Do not assume the current Lambda can run local scripts or reach the host over SSH.
4. Keep the cost-safety audit/notifier **read-only**. Give lifecycle execution a separate least-privilege role and ensure all infrastructure mutations remain represented in Terraform with plan/state locking and an allowlisted plan.
5. Make transitions idempotent and observable: persist or otherwise reconcile the desired/current state, include a stable operation identifier, emit actionable success/failure notifications, and safely handle retries or partial Terraform applies.
6. Document the operator recovery path and update relevant Terraform/script documentation.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A shutdown request only proceeds after the selected idle/expiry policy or an explicit operator request says the Demo should be OFF.
- [ ] Backup failure, invalid manifest, incomplete archive, or failed S3 verification leaves the instance and distribution untouched and emits a useful failure notification.
- [ ] A successful OFF transition applies a Terraform plan that deletes the Demo instance, static IP/network attachment, distribution, and legacy power/start automation, while preserving verified S3 backups and the audit system.
- [ ] The plan policy rejects unexpected resource changes and is safe to retry after interruption.
- [ ] After OFF, AWS inventory confirms the Demo instance, static IP, and distribution are absent; no configured automation starts the Demo; the audit expects `demo_off`.
- [ ] A wake request requires a verified recovery point, recreates and restores the Demo, runs a health check, and only then transitions the desired/audited state to ACTIVE.
- [ ] The notification/audit Lambda cannot stop, start, delete, or otherwise mutate infrastructure. The lifecycle executor uses a separate least-privilege identity.
- [ ] CloudTrail and lifecycle logs make it possible to determine which transition ran, whether backup verification succeeded, what Terraform plan was applied, and why any transition failed, without logging secrets or backup contents.
- [ ] Unit/policy tests cover the state transitions, failed backup gates, retry/partial-apply behavior, and Terraform plan allowlist. Script dry-run and Terraform validation pass. No live AWS mutation is used as a test.

## Relevant code

- `infra/scripts/destroy-demo.sh`
- `infra/scripts/stop-demo.sh`
- `infra/scripts/wake-demo.sh`
- `infra/scripts/lifecycle-guards.sh`
- `infra/terraform/demo/automation.tf`
- `infra/terraform/demo/cost-safety-audit.tf`
- `infra/terraform/demo/web-distribution.tf`
- `infra/terraform/demo/lambda/power_controller.py`
- `infra/terraform/demo/lambda/cost_safety_audit.py`
- `infra/terraform/demo/lambda/test_cost_safety_audit.py`
- `infra/terraform/README.md`

## Out of scope

- Deleting the S3 backup bucket, audit log bucket, or cost-safety audit infrastructure.
- Giving the report-only audit Lambda broad Lightsail/Terraform permissions.
- Replacing verified application backups with an unverified instance deletion or direct console/CLI mutation outside Terraform.

body:
## Objective

Develop and compare **three distinct, end-to-end UI directions** for the current Rewind Demo. Three contributors each own one direction, implement it on a separate branch, review one another's work, and jointly recommend a direction for a later integration decision. The deliverable is a set of runnable, reviewable alternatives backed by firsthand critique and a recorded team decision. This extends the closed, narrower Sprint 0 concept exercise in #11/#12 to the implemented capture-to-reveal journey.

## Product and technical context

Start from current `main`, `README.md`, `DESIGN.md`, and `UX-CONTRACT.md`. The app is an Expo/React Native Demo with Home, Camera, Chat, Archive, and Settings navigation. The defining journey is: enter labelled synthetic Demo access → create/join a group → understand the prompt and sealed cycle → contribute a moment → see its processing/locked state → reveal and view the group film in Archive. Demo access is not authentication; sealed media is not previewable; real and synthetic capture must be labelled accurately.

At kickoff, name the three contributors and their branch ownership in this issue. **Each person owns an entire end-to-end concept**, not a subset of screens. Concept directions must differ in information hierarchy, navigation or interaction model, and visual language; a palette swap does not count as a separate direction.

## Discovery checkpoint: earn the map before redrawing it

The screens and documents are clues, not a substitute for observing the current build. Before proposing layouts, each contributor takes **a different unanswered question** from the list below. The three agree on ownership at kickoff, inspect the current `main` implementation, run the app, and trace the answer from a user action through the relevant state/contract to what appears on screen. Do not assign the same question twice.

- Who is the acting member at each step, and where can that identity change or disappear?
- What is actually sealed before reveal, and what does the UI merely describe as sealed?
- What happens between permission failure, capture/review, and a retryable contribution?
- Which group or cycle state controls what Archive and Chat show, including empty and denied paths?
- Where do local fixture behavior and connected runtime behavior lead to visibly different outcomes?

For the question each person owns, link the current commit, relevant code lines, a firsthand run observation, and the resulting design constraint or unresolved question. A peer must reproduce or challenge the finding in the kickoff/critique thread. If code, contract, and observed UI disagree, record the discrepancy and its impact; if they agree, record the evidence rather than inventing a defect. The concept must explicitly address its owner's finding and the other two findings agreed by the group.

## Work and artifacts required from each contributor

1. **Current-state audit and inspiration.** Personally walk the existing Demo, record the steps and friction in the complete journey, annotate the existing screen/state inventory, and complete the discovery checkpoint above. Collect **six attributed references from at least three products**, with a link or image, the specific interaction or visual principle observed, why it suits or conflicts with Rewind, and any idea deliberately rejected. Identify the user scenario and design principles guiding the concept.
2. **Two divergent rough directions.** Before choosing a detailed concept, produce two end-to-end low-fidelity wireframe sets covering Demo entry/group setup, Home, Camera/contribution, Chat, Archive/reveal, and Settings. Include navigation and the capture-to-sealed-to-reveal transition in both. Explain what is structurally different, show both to the other two contributors, and document why one was advanced. Across the team this yields six rough directions and three selected prototypes.
3. **Selected concept specification.** Provide an annotated task flow and screen map; detailed Android/iOS phone and narrow-web frames; copy and interaction notes; and a state matrix. The state matrix must map relevant loading, empty, permission-denied, failed/retry, processing, locked, and revealed states to the screens and the actor who sees them. Cover both still and clip paths where the interface differs. Record component/token choices and deliberate deviations from `DESIGN.md`; include large-text, focus/keyboard order, accessible names, contrast, and non-colour-only status treatment. Explain which behaviors are already implemented and which are proposals.
4. **Runnable implementation.** Build the selected concept in its own branch (`ui-concept/<owner>-<direction>`) from `main`, using existing Demo fixtures and contracts. Make the key journey locally navigable, including truthful labelled fixture states where needed. Open a draft PR linking this issue. Its description must link the design frames, identify screens/states implemented versus represented by a fixture, give local reproduction steps, and note known gaps.
5. **Personal design record.** Keep a concise decision log linked from the issue or draft PR: question, alternatives considered, evidence or feedback, decision, and resulting revision. Record your own critiques of peer work and your own response to critiques of your work. Each contributor must be able to explain their concept and trade-offs in the live reviews.

Design artifacts may live in a shared design file or in the draft PRs; collect direct links in this issue. Do not create a separate completion/evidence folder. A meeting summary is not a substitute for each person's identifiable contribution.

## Required collaboration checkpoints

1. **Joint kickoff and journey mapping.** The three contributors meet synchronously (in person or on a call), walk the current Demo together, agree on the task script and constraints, and allocate concept ownership. Record attendees, decisions, unresolved questions, and action owners in an issue comment.
2. **Rough-direction critique.** Each person presents both wireframe directions live. Both peers independently give screen-specific feedback and questions on each presenter's work, including at least one challenge about accessibility or truthful product state. Record which direction the owner advanced, what changed because of feedback, and why other suggestions were declined. A comment written solely by the presenter does not count as peer critique.
3. **Prototype review and cross-use.** Each owner demos their branch live. **Both other contributors** independently check out or open that branch and complete the same tasks: find the group prompt and remaining allowance; submit or simulate a contribution and understand its sealed state; find a released film or understand why it is unavailable. Each reviewer records what they actually observed, where they hesitated, an actionable issue or a reason none was found, and whether the setup instructions worked. Owners revise the prototype or document why they did not.
4. **Joint comparison and decision.** After revisions, the three meet again to compare the prototypes against journey clarity, accessibility, phone/web fit, truthful Demo and sealed states, and implementation cost. Record a comparison matrix with evidence links, the preferred direction or unresolved trade-off, what to retain from the alternatives, follow-up tickets, and each person's explicit agreement or dissent. Record attendees, decisions, and action owners in the issue. If opinions differ, preserve the reasons instead of claiming unanimity.

Feedback and walkthrough notes must describe firsthand human observations. AI tools may help produce mockups, code, or draft text, but generated feedback, invented test participants, and automatic sign-offs do not satisfy these checkpoints. Each contributor posts or acknowledges their own critique and final position from their own account.

## Cross-platform test matrix for every concept

After the peer walkthrough and any revisions, test the **same core journey and relevant failure/locked states on each platform**. Browser viewport emulation does not count as Android or iOS testing.

| Platform | Required environment | Required checks |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Android | Physical Android device or Android emulator running the app through Expo Go | Launch/navigation, safe areas and system back, touch targets, keyboard/form behavior, scrolling, capture permission/denied state, labelled fixture path, and sealed/reveal copy. |
| iOS | iPhone 14 or newer simulator through Expo Go | Launch/navigation, safe areas, touch targets, keyboard/form behavior, scrolling, capture permission/denied state, and sealed/reveal copy. |
| Browser 1 | Current Chromium-based browser | Run at a phone-width viewport and a desktop-width viewport; check navigation, keyboard-only path, focus visibility/order, form behavior, overflow, and the shared task script. |
| Browser 2 | A **different browser engine** (Firefox or Safari; another Chromium browser does not count) | Repeat the same phone- and desktop-width checks and record rendering or interaction differences. |

For **each branch and each environment**, link a compact test record in the draft PR or issue: device/emulator model and OS or browser name/version, viewport where relevant, tested commit, task results (pass/fail), defects with reproduction steps, and retest outcome after fixes. Include visual captures for meaningful layout differences and actual error states, using synthetic data only. If a platform cannot be run, mark it **not tested** with the specific blocker; do not substitute screenshots, browser emulation, or agent claims for a device test. The three contributors divide hands-on execution, but the concept owner remains responsible for resolving or explicitly recording findings. Cross-platform UI defects must be fixed on the concept branch or called out as unresolved in the comparison and recommendation.

## Branch and live-app boundary

- Keep the three UI experiments and prototype assets on their separate branches. Do not deploy, change runtime/domain contracts, migrate data, or merge a concept into `main` as part of this issue.
- Keep the existing hosted/local Demo usable. Use synthetic data and avoid real or private media in design artifacts.
- Respect existing navigation, session, capture, chat, reveal, and Archive behavior when describing current functionality. Mark proposed new behavior visibly as a proposal.
- Existing accessibility work in #155 and cycle-history work in #156 remain separate; cite these as dependencies or future opportunities rather than claiming they are complete.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Three named contributors each supply a current-journey audit, a different code-to-screen discovery trace at a cited commit, six annotated references, two structurally distinct complete wireframe directions, and a documented direction choice; peers reproduce or challenge the traces.
- [ ] Three selected concepts each include an annotated flow, screen/state matrix, detailed screens and copy, accessibility/responsive notes, component/token rationale, and a runnable branch with draft PR.
- [ ] The kickoff, rough-direction critique, prototype review, and joint decision are recorded with attendees, concrete decisions, open questions, and action owners.
- [ ] Each contributor gives identifiable, actionable feedback on both peers' rough work and personally tries both peer prototypes using the shared task script. Each owner records revisions or reasons for declining feedback.
- [ ] The shared comparison links evidence to the recommendation, records all three positions, and identifies follow-up implementation work.
- [ ] Each branch reports the actual result of `npm run check` and the four-platform test matrix: Android device/emulator, iPhone 14 or newer simulator, Chromium browser, and Firefox or Safari. Both browsers include phone-width and desktop-width checks. Environment details, task results, defects, fixes/retests, and any untested platform are linked in the issue or draft PR.
- [ ] `main` and the running Demo remain unaffected. Any product-direction choice or merge requires a subsequent scoped implementation decision.

## Review

The three contributors review the synthesis together and can reproduce the peer draft PRs locally. The issue is complete when the artifacts, firsthand cross-reviews, and decision trail are all linked here; a polished prototype alone is insufficient.

server/src/db.ts; server/migrations; server/src/config.ts; server/tests; infra/terraform

## Flow outcome
A new person opens Rewind, sees the brand and welcome route, creates a real account or signs in with an existing account, creates a private four-week group or accepts an invitation, and lands on a truthful group Home. A second account can join; an unrelated account cannot see that group.

## Children
This epic is delivered through focused sub-issues for launch/welcome, credential and session API, login UI/session restore, self-registration, hosted Demo and HTTPS entry, iPhone entry layout and interaction feedback, group creation and Home, invitation creation, and invitation acceptance/privacy. Parent completion requires their integrated hosted web and iPhone journey, not merely isolated screens.

## Acceptance
- A fresh visitor can register a real account and sign in; returning member, expired session, wrong password, offline, and sign-out states lead to the correct screen. Hosted Demo remains usable where advertised.
- Two real accounts, whether self-registered or administrator-created, complete create -> invite -> join on the live dev HTTPS service and on a phone; an invalid/expired invite and cross-group request are denied.
- Current group, prompt, cycle timing, and empty contribution state are visible without synthetic fixtures appearing as real content.
- Demo access remains labelled and separate. No real session is carried in a URL or represented by a Demo profile choice. The iPhone web entry fills the safe viewport and primary actions show immediate progress or failure feedback.

## Outside this epic
Media submission, chat, film release, reminders, MFA, and email-based recovery are separate work. Administrator provisioning remains available for the pilot. The 30 September 2026 self-registration request supersedes the earlier admin-only pilot decision recorded in #169.

## Handoff
Prioritize hosted Demo entry (#304), trusted HTTPS login (#305), and iPhone layout (#306). Build registration API (#307) before the signup UI (#308); interaction feedback (#309) can proceed in parallel. Integrate login and signup before group creation; invitation acceptance closes the epic. Human review is required for authentication, private access, database migration, deployment, and infrastructure PRs.


## Mobile entry issues and source documents
- #304 hosted Demo entry; #305 hosted auth transport; #306 iPhone safe-area layout; #307 real-account registration API; #308 signup UI; #309 press, transition, and loading feedback.
- [Sprint 2 user journey plan](https://github.com/Collaboration95/rewind-app/blob/dev/doc/planning/sprints/sprint-2-user-journey-plan.md) records the earlier admin-only baseline; the issues above record the revised product request.
- [AWS and HTTPS base plan](https://github.com/Collaboration95/rewind-app/blob/dev/doc/planning/sprints/base-plan.md) describes the existing CloudFront/HTTPS boundary; coordinate #305 with #230.

## Reconciled outcome — 2 October 2026
A new or returning member can register/sign in, restore a session, create or join a private 2–10-member group and retain invite intent. Sprint 2 uses the temporary pilot identity; Sprint 3 replaces it with managed OIDC without losing memberships.

## Definition of completion

body:
## Problem

Proposal §5.3 requires relational data to be "backed up using the selected managed database backup mechanism", with provider encryption at rest. The 6 Oct rescope (SQLite stays; fix the daily SQLite upload) is superseded by the 7 Oct decision to deliver PostgreSQL (#261). The SQLite-to-S3 upload itself was fixed in #492 and remains the pre-cutover recovery point. Recovery has never been rehearsed end to end, and RPO/RTO are asserted, not measured.

## Expected

- **Managed backups:** the hosted PostgreSQL database has automatic daily snapshots and point-in-time restore (Lightsail, 7-day retention, encrypted). This is the primary mechanism.
- **Independent copy:** a nightly `pg_dump` (read-only role, verified TLS) goes to the private, versioned, encrypted backup bucket. Each dump is restored into a throwaway server before upload, and its row counts are recorded in a manifest.
- **Rehearsal:** a point-in-time restore runs into a new, isolated database and is verified there. RPO and RTO are measured and recorded, the rehearsal database is deleted, and the live database is never touched.
- **Runbook:** documents cutover rollback, point-in-time recovery, recovery from a lost database, and the SQLite fallback.

## How to check

- After the #261 cutover, run the **Database operations** workflow with `backup`. The S3 prefix gains `rewind-<stamp>.pgdump`, `.media.tar.gz` and `.postgres.json` with `restore_verified: true` and per-table counts.
- Run it with `rehearse-restore`. The job summary shows the recovery point, RPO and RTO, and restored versus live row counts; the rehearsal database is gone afterwards.
- `docs/architecture/postgresql-operations.md` → Recovery matches what the rehearsal did.

Failover (HA standby) is #503; release-environment backups are #504.

**Estimate:** 2–4 focused hours, estimated not measured; integration/device waits excluded.  
**PR batch:** ACCEPTANCE

### Scope and exclusions
Preserve the original acceptance contract and comments. Implementation is already integrated where labelled dev; complete only outstanding acceptance or a reproduced focused defect. Do not reimplement the feature or treat a synthetic check as real acceptance.

### Prerequisites
No unresolved code prerequisite for the bounded local slice; observe the human/resource gate below.

### Observable acceptance
1. Verify each existing acceptance item with exact build/client/data identity and passing relevant checks.
2. Report unavailable account/device/environment as Blocked, not a product failure or pass.
3. Keep the issue open until review, integrated dev and its complete acceptance agree; no closure from merged PR alone.

### Code and artifact boundaries
tests/e2e/production-reset-to-reveal.spec.ts

### Verification contract
Use original issue tests; local real-account browser fixtures first, then consolidate hosted/phone checks as required. Commands are existing/inspected but not run by this planning session unless explicitly labelled proposed. Test names and paths must be rechecked against latest dev before execution.

### Review, resources and stop conditions
Owner previously allowed agent review instead of human peer; label this accurately. Live reset/restart only on authorized synthetic fixture. Do not claim real-group acceptance.

Start from current dev, use Refs #145 in integration PRs targeting dev, retain the current required Quality check and resolved conversations. Before coding, follow skills/agent-solve-issue/SKILL.md and record the actual approach once. Stop on privacy exposure, unexpected destructive/cloud work, conflicting ownership, or a new material scope decision. Bound diagnosis to two focused attempts; do not remove assertions to obtain green results. Completion requires all acceptance, relevant checks, review and integration into dev.

body:
## Summary

The provisioned `rewind-demo` Lightsail host remained in the `running` state because the host-side deployment and safe pause workflow were never installed completely. The approved shutdown controller is behaving as designed: it refuses to stop the instance when the newest S3 backup manifest is older than the permitted 60-minute window.

This incident exposed a gap between the Terraform/AWS foundation and the host deployment. AWS resources exist, but the host is not in a state where `pause-host.sh` can produce a fresh backup and shut the machine down.

Related hosted-runtime work: #101. Related persistence and backup/reset work: #97. Related cost audit: #100.

## Incident evidence

Observed in account region `ap-southeast-1` for the Terraform-managed `rewind-demo` instance:

- Lightsail instance state was `running`.
- The static IP remained attached.
- The newest visible manifest was `rewind-demo/rewind-power-controller-test-20260917T145301Z.manifest.json`, last modified at `2026-09-17T14:53:03Z`.
- Running the approved command with the newest manifest produced:

  ```text
  backup manifest is older than the permitted stop window
  ```

- The controller invocation used the restricted `rewind-demo-operator` profile and did not directly operate Lightsail.
- The Lightsail browser-based SSH terminal could not connect.
- After using the Singapore-region default Lightsail SSH key with the host's allowlisted local SSH path, read-only host inspection succeeded.
- The host-side deployment was incomplete:
  - `/srv/rewind/deploy/pause-host.sh` was missing.
  - `/srv/rewind/rewind.env` was missing.
  - The backup service and timer were not installed in `/etc/systemd/system/`.
  - No Rewind backup timer was enabled or active.
  - No Docker containers were present.
  - No web process was listening on port 80.
  - The expected `/srv/rewind/data`, `/srv/rewind/media`, and `/srv/rewind/backups` directories contained no files during inspection.
  - The deployed directory contained some application and backup artifacts, but not a complete runnable host configuration.

No direct Lightsail stop was performed, and no AWS infrastructure was deleted or modified during this investigation.

## User impact

- The instance can remain running indefinitely because there is no working host-side path that creates a fresh manifest and powers it down.
- The cost-safety audit can correctly report an actionable running demo, but it cannot remediate the condition.
- The approved operator command cannot succeed until the host uploads a fresh manifest.
- The apparent “automatic stop” expectation is incorrect for the current implementation: the checked-in systemd timer is backup-only, and Terraform intentionally defines no automatic stop schedule.
- The host currently appears to be an incomplete deployment rather than a serving Rewind Demo runtime, so the deployment state is misleading.

## Root cause

1. The host deployment copied only part of `deploy/`; `pause-host.sh` was not installed.
2. The host environment file was not created from `rewind.env.example`, so bucket/profile/runtime configuration was absent.
3. The systemd backup unit and timer templates were present in the deployed directory but were never installed and enabled.
4. No end-to-end deployment gate verifies that the runtime, persistent database, backup credentials, timer, and safe pause command are all present before the instance is considered demo-ready.
5. The infrastructure documentation describes a manual backup-gated pause workflow, while the operational expectation was automatic shutdown. There is no explicit schedule implementation for safe automatic pause.
6. SSH recovery is awkward: browser SSH cannot reach the host with the current restricted firewall path, while local SSH required retrieving the regional Lightsail default key.

## Desired behavior

A host must not be considered a ready hosted Demo until it passes a deployment preflight that confirms:

- the runtime is deployed and healthy;
- the persistent database and media paths exist and contain the expected application state;
- the least-privileged host backup identity is configured without secrets in Git;
- `backup.sh` can create and upload the database, media archive, and manifest;
- `pause-host.sh` is installed and executable;
- the backup service/timer is installed and has a successful recent run; and
- a fresh-manifest stop rehearsal has been completed or explicitly recorded as pending.

When an operator requests a pause, the host must back up first, verify the uploaded manifest, stop the runtime, and then shut down the host. The cloud controller must remain fail-closed for missing, malformed, or stale manifests.

## Proposed implementation

### 1. Make host deployment complete and repeatable

- Add a reviewed deployment/bootstrap step that installs the complete `deploy/` set, including `pause-host.sh`.
- Create `/srv/rewind/rewind.env` from the example through an operator-only procedure; keep values and credentials outside Git.
- Create and permission the persistent data, media, and backup directories.
- Ensure ownership and modes match the non-root runtime and the `ubuntu` backup operator.
- Run migrations and start the Compose runtime only after preflight checks pass.

### 2. Install and validate backup automation

- Install `rewind-backup.service` and `rewind-backup.timer`.
- Enable the timer and run one manual backup.
- Verify that the matching database archive, media archive, and manifest appear under the private `rewind-demo/` prefix.
- Confirm that the manifest timestamp is within the controller's configured freshness window.
- Record a non-secret operational result in deployment evidence.

### 3. Define the shutdown schedule explicitly

Choose one supported operating model and document it:

- manual pause through `pause-host.sh`; or
- a reviewed host-side scheduled pause that invokes the backup-gated workflow and shuts down only after backup verification; or
- an explicitly scheduled operator action.

Do not add a blind cloud-side stop schedule that bypasses backup verification. If a scheduled pause is added, make it idempotent, observable, and safe when the runtime/database is unavailable.

### 4. Improve recovery access

- Prefer a managed session path such as SSM if it is intentionally provisioned and audited; otherwise document the regional SSH key and restricted firewall process.
- Keep port 22 restricted to the operator address and do not solve browser SSH failures by leaving SSH open to the world.
- Add a documented, reversible recovery procedure for rotating or replacing the access path.

### 5. Add deployment gates and evidence

- Add an automated host preflight that fails if the runtime, env file, database, backup bucket configuration, or pause script is missing.
- Add a smoke test for a fresh backup followed by `infra/scripts/stop-demo.sh <manifest-key>`.
- Add a negative test proving stale manifests remain rejected.
- Verify the final AWS instance state is `stopped` and that the static IP attachment is understood and documented.
- Ensure the cost-safety audit and deployment status distinguish “provisioned” from “deployed and operational.”

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A clean host deployment installs the complete runtime and all required pause/backup artifacts.
- [ ] `/srv/rewind/rewind.env` is created through a documented secret-safe operator procedure.
- [ ] The runtime serves its health endpoint and the persistent database/media paths are non-empty when the Demo is deployed.
- [ ] The backup timer is installed, enabled, and has a successful recent run.
- [ ] A manual backup uploads matching encrypted database, media, and manifest objects.
- [ ] A manifest within the 60-minute window is accepted by the approved controller and stops only `rewind-demo`.
- [ ] A stale or malformed manifest is rejected and leaves the instance running.
- [ ] The stop workflow is verified end-to-end without using a direct Lightsail stop command.
- [ ] The chosen manual or scheduled pause operating model is documented, including failure behavior and recovery.
- [ ] SSH or managed-session recovery is documented without widening port 22 beyond the operator boundary.
- [ ] Deployment evidence contains no AWS credentials, private keys, Terraform state, or environment-file contents.

## Safety constraints

- Do not delete the instance, static IP, S3 buckets, Lambda, IAM roles, budget, or CloudTrail resources as part of this issue.
- Do not use the direct Lightsail stop API or console Stop button as the normal workflow.
- Do not create a blind automatic stop schedule.
- Keep Terraform as the source of truth for infrastructure and use the approved Terraform/apply review process for infrastructure changes.
- Keep the controller's backup verification gate fail-closed.

## Verification commands

From the operator machine after a successful host backup:

```sh
AWS_PROFILE=rewind-demo-operator \
  ./infra/scripts/stop-demo.sh \
  rewind-demo/rewind-<fresh-timestamp>.manifest.json
```

Then verify the Lightsail instance is `stopped` and the static IP remains attached. Also verify that a deliberately stale manifest still returns the expected freshness error.

- No Lightsail managed database, load balancer, NAT gateway, always-on worker, or real/personal media in Sprint 2.

## Objective and value

Make the still capture screen reachable on a physical iOS or Android device. Verified defect from the PR #80 review at head `3769463`.

## Problem

`src/capture/platform.ts:41` gates capture on `await CameraView.isAvailableAsync()`, but that static is web-only in `expo-camera@57.0.4`: `src/CameraView.tsx:86-93` marks it `@platform web` and throws `UnavailabilityError` when the native manager does not implement it. The native modules register only `isModernBarcodeScannerAvailable` and `toggleRecordingAsyncAvailable` (`ios/CameraViewModule.swift:33,37`; `android/.../CameraViewModule.kt:73,78`), and no `isAvailableAsync` registration exists on either platform.

The throw is caught by the bare `catch` at `src/capture/platform.ts:54`, which returns `{ camera: 'undecided', microphone: 'undecided' }`. The screen then parks on `capability-undecided` (`src/capture/CameraCaptureScreen.tsx:263-273`) whose only action, `Check again`, re-runs the same failing probe. Granting permissions through `requestAccess` does not establish availability either, so with `EXPO_PUBLIC_CAMERA_MODE` unset there is no in-app path to the shutter on a device. Reproduced under jest with the native surface emulated as the two registered properties: control (probe injected) shows the shutter, native surface shows `camera-capability-undecided` and the shutter never appears. `EXPO_PUBLIC_CAMERA_MODE=demo` and test-injected platforms bypass the probe and are unaffected.

## In scope

- Feature-detect `isAvailableAsync` before calling it and treat a missing native probe as available, or let the permission request establish availability on native.
- Coverage for the native surface (probe missing) case.

## Out of scope

- Recording, upload or reveal work; camera quality tuning.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] On a physical device with granted permissions the capture control is reachable.
- [ ] A missing native capability export no longer produces a permanent `capability-undecided` state.
- [ ] The simulated fixture path and its honest labeling are unchanged.

## Relevant areas

- `src/capture/platform.ts`
- `src/capture/CameraCaptureScreen.tsx`
- `tests/capture-platform.test.ts`

Dependencies:
- PR #80 (head `3769463`), issue #40.

Risk: High (capture is unreachable on the supported device target).

## Verification

## Objective and value

Stop the local runtime from answering 500 and logging a stack trace for a malformed request path. Verified defect from the PR #80 review at head `3769463`.

## Problem

`decodeURIComponent` is called on raw path segments at `server/src/http.ts:217` (`/sessions/:id`), `379` (`/groups/:id`), `411` (`/messages/:id`), `431` (`/contributions/:id`) and `448` (`/clips|/films|/downloads/:id`), and a sequence such as `%E0%A4%A` makes it throw `URIError`. The pattern `[^/]+?` lets any client send that segment, and the throw escapes `handleRequest` into the wrapper in `createRuntimeServer` (`http.ts:458-471`), which logs a stack trace and answers `500 internal_error`. Reproduced in-process at this head for `/sessions/%E0%A4%A`, `/groups/%E0%A4%A`, `/messages/%E0%A4%A`, `/contributions/%E0%A4%A` and the clip, film and download families: six call sites across five route families.

## In scope

- Decode segments through one shared helper that maps `URIError` to a 400 `invalid_request` response.

## Out of scope

- The generic error wrapper and its logging.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] A malformed segment on each exposed route family returns 400 `invalid_request`, not 500.
- [x] No stack trace is logged for a client-supplied malformed segment.
- [x] Valid and percent-encoded ids keep working.

## Relevant areas

- `server/src/http.ts`
- `server/tests/runtime.test.mjs`

## Dependencies and risk

Dependencies:
- PR #80 (head `3769463`).

Risk: Medium (any LAN peer can generate log noise and 500s on the default 0.0.0.0 bind).

## Verification

- `npm run server:test` with malformed-segment cases.

## Stop conditions

Stop if the fix changes resource-authorization ordering; the decode must stay after route matching but before resource lookup.

## Note (lower severity, same review)

`requestBody` (`server/src/http.ts:99-117`) returns early at line 105 when a body exceeds 64 KiB; the async iterator then destroys the request with `ABORT_ERR` instead of draining it. At this head the client still receives the documented `400 invalid_demo_access` in the tested Node runtime, so no client-visible break was reproduced; draining with `request.resume()` before responding is recommended hygiene and can be handled in the same change or a follow-up.

## Objective and value

Close the three lower-severity defects the PR #80 review found alongside the functional bugs, so the checks stay honest and the capsule stops refetching on unrelated context updates. Verified at head `3769463`.

## Problem 1: runtime repositories are rebuilt every render

`App.tsx:120-121` calls `createRuntimeRepositories(runtimeClient, session.id)` in the `SessionGate` render body, so `CapsuleProvider` receives fresh repository objects whenever the session context changes. Its `load` callback depends on `[cycleRepository, groupRepository, memberId]` (`src/capsule/CapsuleProvider.tsx:52-98`), so the effect re-runs, resets to `loading` and refetches the group and cycle. Probe: selecting the already-selected member (no session change) took `getGroupForMember` calls from 1 to 3. Fix: `useMemo` on `[runtimeClient, session.id]`.

## Problem 2: the actor-switch assertion passes without a switch

## Objective and value

Make the active session the single source of truth for the acting member and group in the offline demo path. Two related verified defects from the PR #80 review at head `3769463`.

## Problem 1: offline group and role resolution

`src/data/demo-repository.ts:90-97` scans locally created groups first and returns the first one containing the member with a hardcoded `actingMemberRole: 'owner'`, before it considers the seeded group (lines 99-107). With the runtime unavailable (the case this repository exists for), a member whose session is attached to `demo-group` is shown whichever local group they were added to, with a role they may not hold. Probe: create `Saturday table`, sign out, re-enter as `demo-1`; the session carries `demo-group` but Home renders `Saturday table`.

## Problem 2: picker and session disagree

`DemoProfilePicker` stays consistent only because its own `onPress` calls both `selectMember` and, when a session is active, `demoSession.chooseMember` (`src/profiles/DemoProfilePicker.tsx:40-41`). The entry screen calls `chooseMember(profile.id)` alone (`App.tsx:261`), so entering as Birch leaves the selection store on Amber; the picker then renders `Current member: Amber` (`DemoProfilePicker.tsx:28`), marks Amber selected, and the offline resolution above is fed a member that does not match the session actor. Probe: session actor Birch, selection store null, picker shows Amber.

## In scope

- Prefer the session group id and fall back to the membership scan only when the session carries no group; derive the role from the resolved group rather than a hardcoded value.

## Out of scope

- Server-side membership policy.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] With no runtime, a session attached to `demo-group` resolves to `demo-group` and its correct role even when other local groups contain the member.

- [x] Existing local group creation and offline tests pass.
