body:
## Objective and value

Close the one state-changing owner-only route that can be driven with a guessable member id instead of a validated Demo session. Verified defect from the PR #80 review at head `3769463` (base `f3691e5`).

## Problem

`server/src/http.ts:331` selects the actor with

```ts
const memberId = sessionId ? sessionMember(database, url) : actingMember(url);
```

so a request that omits `sessionId` (or sends an empty value) falls back to the `memberId` query parameter and is treated as an authenticated actor. Driving the compiled handler in-process at this head:

- `POST /cycles/demo/advance?groupId=demo-group&memberId=demo-1&advanceSeconds=60` with no session returns `200`, moves the `demo-cycle` boundaries and appends a `cycle_control_events` row.
- The same call with `memberId=demo-2` returns the safe `403` denial, and any invalid `sessionId` is rejected, so only the omitted parameter bypasses authorization.
- Every other write route already requires a session: `POST /groups` returns 403 without one (`http.ts:270-275`) and `POST /demo/reset` returns 401 `session_required` (`http.ts:256-264`).

`GET /profiles` is unauthenticated and returns the synthetic member ids (`server/src/http.ts:323-326`); `demo-1` is also the hardcoded default in `src/data/demo-repository.ts:19`. The runtime binds `0.0.0.0:8787` by default (`server/src/config.ts:4-5`) and `/health` advertises the Mac LAN URL (`server/src/http.ts:145-159`), so any host on the trusted LAN can drive the demo cycle.

## In scope

- Require a valid session for `POST /cycles/demo/advance`, derive the actor from the session only, and answer 401 `session_required` when it is missing (matching `/demo/reset`).
- Regression coverage for the omitted, empty and invalid `sessionId` cases.

## Out of scope

- The unauthenticated read routes and the synthetic identity model itself.
- Cloud or account authentication.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] `POST /cycles/demo/advance` without a valid `sessionId` returns 401 `session_required` and mutates nothing.
- [x] `memberId` is ignored for actor selection on that route.
- [x] Server tests cover omitted, empty and invalid session values, plus the existing owner and non-owner cases.

## Relevant areas

- `server/src/http.ts`
- `server/tests/cycles.test.mjs`

## Dependencies and risk

Dependencies:
- PR #80 (head `3769463`), issue #53.

Risk: High (LAN-reachable authorization bypass).

## Verification

- `npm run server:test` with the new denial cases.

## Stop conditions

Stop if the fix would change the demo identity model for read routes; keep the change scoped to this write route.

title: BUG: Demo cycle advance is reachable without a session (P1)

body:
## Objective and value

Let a demonstrator always end Demo access and reset local data, even when the local runtime rejects the request. Verified defect from the PR #80 review at head `3769463`.

## Problem

`src/session/DemoSessionProvider.tsx:183-204`: `signOut` awaits `runtimeClient.invalidateDemoSession(session.id)` inside the same `try` as `store.clear()`; the `catch` at line 196 sets `status: 'active'`, so every `LocalRuntimeError` keeps the session and skips the local clear. The same pattern repeats in `resetDemoData` (lines 206-232), where a rejected `runtimeClient.resetDemoData` additionally skips `resetCaptureData()`, `resetLocalDemoData()`, `localGroupStore.clear()`, `selectionStore.clear()` and `store.clear()`.

Verified with a fake runtime client rejecting with `LocalRuntimeError('Demo access was not found.', 404)` (the shape produced after a runtime restart or database reset): the status stayed `active` and the session record stayed in AsyncStorage; with a pre-seeded local group and selection, the reset left both stored. The restore path already encodes the intended policy at lines 124-132 (clear local state on 401 or 404), and `resetDemoData` is the operator recovery action, so it must not depend on the runtime.

Correction to the review text: `DELETE /sessions/:id` returns `409 already_inactive` for an invalidated session and `404 not_found` for an unknown id (401 applies to `GET` on an invalidated or expired session, not to DELETE of an unknown id).

## In scope

- Treat 401, 404, 409 and an unreachable runtime as "clear locally and continue" in both mutations, matching the restore path.
- Coverage for a rejecting runtime client in sign-out and reset.

## Out of scope

- Runtime-side session semantics; those are already idempotent.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] Sign-out returns to clean entry and clears the stored session even when the runtime rejects the invalidation.
- [x] Reset clears the session, local groups, profile selection and capture data even when the runtime rejects the reset.
- [x] A genuinely reachable runtime still invalidates the session server-side.

## Relevant areas

- `src/session/DemoSessionProvider.tsx`
- `tests/identity-groups-settings.test.tsx`

## Dependencies and risk

Dependencies:
- PR #80 (head `3769463`), issues #35 and #39.

Risk: High (a stuck Demo session can only be cleared by wiping app storage).

## Verification

- Focused Jest coverage with a rejecting runtime client plus the existing settings lifecycle tests.

## Stop conditions

Stop if clearing locally would leave a server-side session that the app then reuses; the restore path must keep rejecting it.

body:
## Objective and value

Create a small, reviewable UI direction for the flows required by Sprint 0 and the forecast Sprint 1 slice, so the team can converge on an implementable experience before adding feature depth.

## Screens and concepts

Iterate on at least two distinct concepts for each of these three areas:

1. Home / group capsule: group name, prompt, cycle countdown, contribution quota, and locked-state messaging.
2. Local demo profile switcher: five synthetic members, current-actor state, and explicit `Local demo` labelling.
3. Camera entry / permission flow: permission explanation, unavailable/denied state, and the later capture-entry path; recording itself remains a Sprint 1 implementation decision.

The team may explore a Settings screen only if a confirmed Sprint 0 or Sprint 1 requirement is identified; it is not assumed by this ticket.

## In scope

- Low- to mid-fidelity wireframes or prototypes for the three areas above.
- A short comparison of the alternatives and a recorded selection/rationale.
- Responsive/layout notes for the supported demo platform.
- Accessibility notes for hierarchy, focus/keyboard behaviour where supported, larger text, contrast, and non-colour state communication.
- Mapping of selected screens to the acceptance criteria in issues #5, #6, #7, and the Sprint 1 capture/permission forecast.
- Prototype frames or a shared design link, because the concepts themselves are this ticket’s deliverable.

## Out of scope

- Production UI implementation or a design-system rewrite.
- Authentication, cloud services, recording, upload, video processing, chat, reveal, archive media, or final visual polish.
- Treating local demo profiles as secure accounts or private multi-user data.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Two or more distinct concepts are shown for each of the three required areas.
- [ ] The team records the selected direction and the reasons for rejecting alternatives.
- [ ] The selected direction covers the happy path plus loading, empty, unavailable/denied, and locked-safe states relevant to Sprint 0/Sprint 1.
- [ ] The selected direction uses honest `Local demo` wording and does not imply authentication, privacy, or implemented future features.
- [ ] Accessibility and supported-platform constraints are recorded and reviewable.
- [ ] Selected directions and follow-up implementation tickets are recorded in this issue without silently changing the Sprint 0 commitment.

## Verification

Peer walkthrough with the Sprint 0 acceptance lead and UX/accessibility reviewer; check each concept against the linked issue criteria and link the prototype frames. No separate evidence folder or completion note is required.

## Proposed timebox

4 team-hours from contingency only, unless the team explicitly re-plans Sprint 0 capacity. This ticket remains Product Backlog until that decision is made.

## Stop conditions

Stop and escalate if the supported platform, Sprint 1 capture scope, lecturer expectations, or a product/privacy decision changes the required screens materially.

title: US-01 task: Add reachable main navigation

body:
## User story

As a Rewind group member, I want to see the current prompt, time remaining and my contribution allowance so that I know what kind of moment to capture and how much I may still contribute without seeing locked media.

## Value

Demonstrates the defining delayed-reveal group experience rather than only a generic navigation shell.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] Given a selected synthetic group member, when Home loads, then it shows the group name, current prompt, and cycle time remaining.
- [x] Given the member has no contributions, when Home loads, then it shows `0 of 5 contributions` and `0 of 30 seconds` remaining/used in clear wording.
- [x] Given seeded contribution metadata changes, when Home reloads, then quota values come from the shared domain/repository boundary rather than separately hard-coded UI values.
- [x] Given the cycle is collecting and contributions are locked, when Home renders, then no unrevealed media URI, thumbnail, image, video player, or share action is present.
- [x] Given data is loading, missing, or recoverably fails, when Home renders, then the member sees an understandable loading, empty, or retry state.
- [x] Given a screen reader or larger text setting, when the member reads the countdown and quota, then equivalent text is available and state is not communicated by colour alone.

## Not included

- Recording or submitting a contribution.
- Delete/recapture and processing/retry policy.
- A real four-week scheduler or server-generated countdown.
- Revealing or playing media.

## Estimate and ownership

Story points: 8. Lead: B. Reviewer: E. Target: Week 2.

## Verification

Repository-backed quota test, locked-media negative rendering test, and loading/empty/retry/large-text/screen-reader checks.

## Stop conditions

Stop for a data-contract decision that would require hard-coded UI values or expose locked media.

title: US-03: Understand the current group capsule

body:
## User story

As a Rewind demo participant, I want to choose one of the five sample member profiles so that I can experience group behaviour from that member's point of view before real sign-in is implemented.

## Value

Establishes the actor used by group, contribution, and later chat stories without misrepresenting local data as authentication.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] Given a clean local reset, when Rewind starts, then exactly five synthetic member profiles and one synthetic group are available.
- [x] Given the profile switcher is open, when the participant selects a different member, then the visible current actor changes immediately.
- [x] Given a member was selected, when the application is relaunched, then the agreed default or last selection is restored consistently.
- [x] Given any profile-selection screen is visible, then it is labelled `Local demo` or equivalent and never uses language such as secure login, authenticated user, or private account.
- [x] Given a synthetic actor who is not a group member, when group data is requested, then the membership guard refuses access in an automated negative test.

## Not included

- OIDC, Cognito, passwords, or real identity.
- Creating or editing profiles, avatars, or account deletion.
- Real invitation acceptance or multi-device membership.

## Estimate and ownership

Story points: 5. Lead: A. Reviewer: C. Target: Week 2.

## Verification

Reset-fixture, profile-selection/relaunch, and negative membership-guard tests.

## Stop conditions

Stop for a local data-contract or membership-policy decision that would change the implementation.
